objects.description: Built-in C99/C++ boolean type imported via <stdbool.h>. This is not a custom type defined in this header and should generally be ignored per instructions. Included here only to note there are no custom types defined in this header.

objects.definition: typedef struct _cups_array_s cups_array_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a CUPS sorted array. The underlying struct _cups_array_s is not defined in this header, so the type is used as an opaque pointer for managing a sorted array of elements via the provided API. Construction and destruction are done through cupsArrayNew3/cupsArrayDelete and related helpers. Internal layout and fields are intentionally hidden.

objects.definition: typedef int (*cups_array_cb_t)(void *first, void *second, void *data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for array comparison callbacks used to order elements. Returns an int like strcmp: <0 if first < second, 0 if equal, >0 if first > second. The data parameter is the user context pointer passed at array creation.

objects.definition: typedef int (*cups_ahash_cb_t)(void *element, void *data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for hashing elements when hash indexing is enabled. Should return a non-negative hash value based on the element and optional user data.

objects.definition: typedef void *(*cups_acopy_cb_t)(void *element, void *data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for copying elements when the array needs to duplicate stored items (e.g., during duplication). Should return a newly allocated copy of element using data as context.

objects.definition: typedef void (*cups_afree_cb_t)(void *element, void *data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for freeing elements stored in the array. Called by the array when elements are removed or when the array is destroyed, using data as context.

objects.definition: typedef off_t ssize_t;
objects.description: Alias for off_t used on Windows where ssize_t is not available. Represents a signed size/offset type. Only defined when _WIN32 is set and __CUPS_SSIZE_T_DEFINED is not already defined.

objects.definition: typedef struct _cups_file_s cups_file_t;
objects.description: Opaque CUPS file handle type used by the CUPS file API for file I/O with optional compression handling. The underlying struct _cups_file_s is not defined in this header, making this an opaque handle managed via the provided API functions.

objects.definition: typedef struct _cups_dir_s cups_dir_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle for enumerating entries in a directory via the CUPS directory APIs. The actual structure is not defined in this header (incomplete type); it is managed through the provided functions to open, read, rewind, and close a directory stream.

Concrete directory entry record returned by cupsDirRead. Contains the entry’s filename (up to 259 characters plus NUL) and a POSIX stat structure with metadata for the file. Instances are typically owned/managed by the directory stream and may be reused between reads; persist data by copying if needed.

  HTTP_STATUS_CONTINUE = 100,		// Everything OK, keep going...

  HTTP_STATUS_CREATED,			// PUT command was successful
  HTTP_STATUS_ACCEPTED,			// DELETE command was successful
  HTTP_STATUS_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE,	// Information isn't authoritative

  HTTP_STATUS_MULTI_STATUS,		// Multiple status codes (WebDAV)
  HTTP_STATUS_ALREADY_REPORTED,		// Already reported (WebDAV)

  HTTP_STATUS_MULTIPLE_CHOICES = 300,	// Multiple files match request

  HTTP_STATUS_PAYMENT_REQUIRED,		// Payment required

  HTTP_STATUS_LENGTH_REQUIRED,		// A content length or encoding is required
  HTTP_STATUS_PRECONDITION,		// Precondition failed
  HTTP_STATUS_CONTENT_TOO_LARGE,	// Content too large

				// Precondition required (WebDAV)

  HTTP_STATUS_REQUEST_HEADER_FIELDS_TOO_LARGE = 431,
				// Request Header Fields Too Large (WebDAV)

functions.name: cupsArrayAdd
functions.description: Adds an element to the array according to the array’s sort/compare function. Returns an integer status (exact semantics not documented here). Use on arrays created by cupsArrayNew3 (or deprecated constructors).
requirements: a must be a valid, initialized cups_array_t* created by cupsArrayNew3 or the deprecated constructors.
e must be a pointer to an element type compatible with the array’s comparison (and hash, if any) callbacks; the compare function must be able to compare e against existing elements.
If a copy callback was supplied at creation, the element may be copied; if not, the stored pointer may be the same as e (ownership semantics depend on callbacks).

functions.name: cupsArrayAddStrings
functions.signature: bool cupsArrayAddStrings(cups_array_t *a, const char *s, char delim);
functions.description: Tokenizes the input string s on delimiter delim and adds each token as a string element to the array. Returns true/false status (exact success/failure conditions not documented here).
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t* intended to store C-strings (char*), ideally created with copy/free callbacks suitable for string storage.
s must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string.
delim specifies the single-character delimiter used to split s.

functions.name: cupsArrayClear
functions.description: Removes all elements from the array, resetting its contents. If a free callback was provided at creation, it will be invoked for each removed element.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Callers should assume previously returned element pointers become invalid after clearing if a free callback is in use.

functions.name: cupsArrayCount
functions.description: Deprecated. Returns the number of elements in the array. Use cupsArrayGetCount instead.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Prefer cupsArrayGetCount for new code.

functions.name: cupsArrayCurrent
functions.description: Deprecated. Returns the current element according to the array’s internal iterator. Use cupsArrayGetCurrent instead.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
The internal iterator position must have been established (e.g., by a prior First/Next/Prev/Get* call); otherwise this may return NULL.

functions.name: cupsArrayDelete
functions.description: Destroys the array and releases its resources. If a free callback was provided, it is called for any stored elements as needed.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t* or NULL.
After calling, a and any iterators derived from it must no longer be used.

functions.name: cupsArrayDup
functions.description: Creates a duplicate of the array. Element duplication behavior depends on the copy/free callbacks configured for the source array (deep vs. shallow copy unknown here).
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
If the array was created without a copy callback, duplicated array may share element pointers with the original; callers must manage lifetimes accordingly (exact semantics not documented).

functions.name: cupsArrayFind
functions.description: Searches the array for an element equal to e using the array’s compare (and optionally hash) functions. Returns the stored matching element pointer or NULL if not found.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
e must be comparable by the array’s comparison callback to the stored elements.

functions.name: cupsArrayFirst
functions.description: Deprecated. Positions the internal iterator at the first element and returns it. Use cupsArrayGetFirst instead.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Returns NULL if the array is empty.

functions.name: cupsArrayGetCount
functions.description: Returns the number of elements currently stored in the array.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.

functions.name: cupsArrayGetCurrent
functions.description: Returns the current element according to the array’s internal iterator without changing the iterator position.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Returns NULL if there is no current element (e.g., before iteration or after the end).

functions.name: cupsArrayGetElement
functions.description: Returns the element at index n. Indexing base (0- or 1-based) is not specified here.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
n must be within the valid index range for the array; out-of-range indices return NULL (exact behavior not documented).

functions.name: cupsArrayGetFirst
functions.description: Positions the internal iterator to the first element and returns it.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Returns NULL if the array is empty.

functions.name: cupsArrayGetIndex
functions.description: Returns the current iterator index within the array. Exact meaning when no current element is selected is not specified here.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
If there is no current element, the returned value’s meaning is unspecified in this header (may be negative or implementation-defined).

functions.name: cupsArrayGetInsert
functions.description: Returns the current insertion index or position used by the last search/operation (exact semantics not documented in this header).
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Interpretation of the returned index depends on recent operations; specifics are not documented here.

functions.name: cupsArrayGetLast
functions.description: Positions the internal iterator to the last element and returns it.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Returns NULL if the array is empty.

functions.name: cupsArrayGetNext
functions.description: Advances the internal iterator to the next element and returns it.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Call after GetFirst/GetCurrent/GetPrev/etc.; returns NULL when the end is reached.

functions.name: cupsArrayGetPrev
functions.description: Moves the internal iterator to the previous element and returns it.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Call after establishing a current position; returns NULL when the beginning is passed.

functions.name: cupsArrayGetUserData
functions.description: Returns the user data pointer that was supplied when the array was created.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
User data is opaque; callers must cast to the appropriate type as needed.

functions.name: cupsArrayIndex
functions.description: Returns the element at index n. This appears to be an index-based accessor similar to cupsArrayGetElement.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
n must be within the valid index range; behavior for out-of-range indices is unspecified here.

functions.name: cupsArrayInsert
functions.description: Inserts an element into the array. The distinction from Add is not documented here; both place an element according to the array’s ordering.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
e must be compatible with the array’s compare (and hash, if set) functions.
If a copy callback is configured, insertion may copy the element; otherwise the original pointer may be stored.

functions.name: cupsArrayLast
functions.description: Deprecated. Positions the internal iterator at the last element and returns it. Use cupsArrayGetLast instead.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Returns NULL if the array is empty.

functions.name: cupsArrayNew
functions.description: Deprecated. Creates a new array using comparison callback f and associates user data d with the array. Use cupsArrayNew3 instead.
requirements: f should be a valid comparison function that imposes a total order on elements handled by the array.
d is an opaque user data pointer passed to callbacks.
Prefer cupsArrayNew3 for new code.

functions.name: cupsArrayNew2
functions.signature: cups_array_t *cupsArrayNew2(cups_array_cb_t f, void *d, cups_ahash_cb_t h, int hsize);
functions.description: Deprecated. Creates a new array with comparison callback f, user data d, and optional hashing support via h and hsize. Use cupsArrayNew3 instead.
requirements: f should be a valid comparison function for the stored elements.
If h is provided, it must be compatible with the comparison function and the element type; hsize should be a positive hash table size.
d is an opaque user data pointer passed to callbacks.
Prefer cupsArrayNew3 for new code.

functions.name: cupsArrayNew3
functions.signature: cups_array_t *cupsArrayNew3(cups_array_cb_t f, void *d, cups_ahash_cb_t h, int hsize, cups_acopy_cb_t cf, cups_afree_cb_t ff);
functions.description: Creates a new array with a comparison callback f and optional user data d. Optional hash function h with table size hsize can accelerate lookups. Optional copy callback cf and free callback ff control element ownership and lifecycle.
requirements: f should be a valid comparison function defining a strict weak ordering for the stored elements; callers should not pass NULL unless the implementation explicitly allows it.
If h is provided, hsize should be a positive integer; h must be consistent with f (elements that compare equal should hash equal).
If cf is provided, it must return a pointer suitable for storage and later release by ff; if ff is provided, it must be able to free elements produced by cf.
d is an opaque user data pointer provided to callbacks.

functions.name: cupsArrayNewStrings
functions.description: Creates a new array of strings by splitting the input string s around delimiter delim and storing each token as a string element.
requirements: s must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string.
delim is the single-character delimiter used to split s.
Resulting array stores strings (likely char*); memory ownership and copy/free behavior are defined by the implementation (not specified here).

functions.name: cupsArrayNext
functions.description: Deprecated. Advances the internal iterator to the next element and returns it. Use cupsArrayGetNext instead.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Returns NULL when the end is reached.

functions.name: cupsArrayPrev
functions.description: Deprecated. Moves the internal iterator to the previous element and returns it. Use cupsArrayGetPrev instead.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Returns NULL when the beginning is passed.

functions.name: cupsArrayRemove
functions.description: Removes an element equal to e from the array using the array’s comparison (and possibly hash) functions. Returns an integer status (exact semantics not documented).
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
e must be comparable by the array’s comparison callback to the stored elements.
If a free callback was provided at creation, it may be called for the removed element.

functions.name: cupsArrayRestore
functions.description: Restores a previously saved iterator position and returns the current element at that restored position. Works in conjunction with cupsArraySave.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
A prior call to cupsArraySave should have saved a position; behavior is unspecified if no position was saved.
May return NULL if the restored position is invalid or the array has changed.

functions.name: cupsArraySave
functions.description: Saves the current iterator position onto an internal stack so it can be restored later with cupsArrayRestore. Returns an integer status (exact semantics not documented).
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Saving and restoring positions when the array is modified between calls may yield unspecified results.

functions.name: cupsArrayUserData
functions.description: Deprecated. Returns the user data pointer associated with the array. Use cupsArrayGetUserData instead.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.

functions.name: cupsFileClose
functions.description: Closes a CUPS file handle previously opened with cupsFileOpen, cupsFileOpenFd, or one of the standard stream accessors. Frees associated resources and flushes any buffered output as needed. Returns an integer status (exact semantics not documented here).
requirements: fp must be a valid, open cups_file_t* obtained from this API
fp must not be NULL
After a successful call, fp must not be used again

functions.name: cupsFileCompression
functions.description: Deprecated: Retrieves the compression setting for a CUPS file. The header marks this as deprecated with guidance to use cupsFileIsCompressed instead. Return value semantics are not documented here.
requirements: fp must be a valid, open cups_file_t*
fp must not be NULL
Prefer using cupsFileIsCompressed(fp) instead

functions.name: cupsFileEOF
functions.description: Tests for end-of-file on a CUPS file stream. Returns a nonzero/zero integer indicating EOF status (exact values not documented here).
requirements: fp must be a valid, open cups_file_t*
fp must not be NULL

functions.name: cupsFileFind
functions.signature: const char *cupsFileFind(const char *filename, const char *path, int executable, char *buffer, int bufsize);
functions.description: Searches for a file named filename within a search path string path, optionally requiring that the target be executable. On success returns a pointer (likely to buffer) with the resolved path. Buffer and length are supplied by the caller. Exact search rules and return semantics are not documented in this header.
requirements: filename must be a non-NULL string
path must be a non-NULL string containing one or more search directories (format unspecified)
buffer must be a non-NULL writable character array
bufsize must be a positive integer specifying the size of buffer in bytes and must be large enough to hold the resulting path including null-terminator
executable is an int flag; meaning inferred as whether to require executability but exact accepted values are not documented

functions.name: cupsFileFlush
functions.description: Flushes buffered output for a CUPS file stream to the underlying file descriptor. Returns an integer status (exact semantics not documented here).
requirements: fp must be a valid, open cups_file_t* in a writable mode
fp must not be NULL

functions.name: cupsFileGetChar
functions.description: Reads the next character from a CUPS file stream and returns it as an unsigned char cast to int, or an error/EOF indicator (exact values not documented here).
requirements: fp must be a valid, open cups_file_t* in a readable mode
fp must not be NULL

functions.name: cupsFileGetConf
functions.signature: char *cupsFileGetConf(cups_file_t *fp, char *buf, size_t buflen, char **value, int *linenum);
functions.description: Parses the next configuration directive line from a CUPS configuration-style text file. Likely splits a directive and its value, returns the directive in buf and sets *value to the value portion. Updates *linenum with the current line number. Exact parsing rules and return semantics are not provided in this header.
requirements: fp must be a valid, open cups_file_t* in a readable mode
buf must be a non-NULL writable buffer with length buflen
buflen must be greater than 0 and sufficient for the line and terminating null
value may be NULL if the caller does not need the value; if non-NULL it must be a valid char**
linenum may be NULL if the caller does not need line numbers; if non-NULL it must be a valid int*

functions.name: cupsFileGetLine
functions.description: Reads a line of text from a CUPS file stream into buf, up to buflen bytes, and returns the number of bytes stored (exact inclusion of terminator not documented here). Handles CUPS text line conventions (e.g., various line endings).
requirements: fp must be a valid, open cups_file_t* in a readable mode
buf must be a non-NULL writable buffer
buflen must be greater than 0

functions.name: cupsFileGets
functions.description: Reads a line from a CUPS file stream into buf, similar to fgets, returning buf on success or NULL on failure/EOF (exact semantics not documented here). Handles CUPS-supported line endings.
requirements: fp must be a valid, open cups_file_t* in a readable mode
buf must be a non-NULL writable buffer
buflen must be greater than 0

functions.name: cupsFileIsCompressed

functions.signature: void cupsOAuthSaveClientData(const char *auth_uri, const char *redirect_uri, const char *client_id, const char *client_secret);

functions.name: cupsLangDefault
functions.description: Returns a cups_lang_t handle for the current process locale (the default language), using an internal cache. Typical usage is to obtain this handle once and use it to query localization data (for example, encoding) and then release it when finished.
requirements: Callers should check the return value for NULL to handle allocation or lookup failures (not explicitly documented; inferred safe practice).

Every successful call that returns a non-NULL cups_lang_t must be paired with exactly one call to cupsLangFree to release the handle back to the cache (inferred from presence of cupsLangFree and cached design).
The returned pointer remains valid until it is released with cupsLangFree or globally invalidated by cupsLangFlush.
Do not use the returned pointer after calling cupsLangFree or after a cupsLangFlush.

functions.name: cupsLangEncoding
functions.description: Returns the name of the text encoding for the specified language handle (for example, "UTF-8"). Intended for callers that need the character encoding associated with a cups_lang_t obtained via cupsLangGet or cupsLangDefault.
requirements: lang must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid cups_lang_t previously obtained from cupsLangGet or cupsLangDefault.
Do not use lang if it has been released with cupsLangFree or invalidated by cupsLangFlush.
The returned string is read-only and owned by the library; do not modify or free it.
The lifetime of the returned pointer is tied to the validity of lang; it may become invalid once lang is freed or flushed.

functions.name: cupsLangFlush
functions.description: Flushes the internal language cache, releasing any cached cups_lang_t entries. Use to force reloading of language resources or to free memory.
requirements: After calling this function, any cups_lang_t pointers previously returned by cupsLangGet or cupsLangDefault become invalid and must not be used.
Only call when it is safe to invalidate all outstanding cups_lang_t handles in the process (e.g., no other code retains or uses them).
This function takes no arguments and returns no status; callers cannot detect errors from the API (behavior on failure is unknown).

functions.name: cupsLangFree
functions.description: Releases a cups_lang_t handle obtained from cupsLangGet or cupsLangDefault back to the internal cache. After this call, the handle must not be used.
requirements: lang must be a valid pointer previously returned by cupsLangGet or cupsLangDefault.
Do not call with pointers that were not obtained from this API, and do not use the pointer after this call.
Each successful acquisition of a cups_lang_t (via cupsLangGet or cupsLangDefault) must be released exactly once with cupsLangFree (no double-free, no leaks).
Passing NULL is not documented; callers should avoid passing NULL (behavior unknown).

functions.name: cupsLangGet
functions.description: Returns a cups_lang_t handle for the specified language/locale name, using an internal cache. Typical inputs resemble locale or language tags such as "en", "en_US", or "fr_FR.UTF-8". Use the returned handle to query localization-related properties and release it when done.
requirements: language must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string naming a language/locale (exact accepted formats are not documented; typical locale or BCP 47–style tags are expected based on the name and context).
Callers should check the return value for NULL to handle lookup or allocation failures (not explicitly documented; inferred safe practice).
Every successful call that returns a non-NULL cups_lang_t must be paired with exactly one call to cupsLangFree to release the handle back to the cache.
The returned pointer remains valid until it is released with cupsLangFree or globally invalidated by cupsLangFlush.
Do not use the returned pointer after calling cupsLangFree or after a cupsLangFlush.

functions.name: ippAddBoolean
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddBoolean(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, const char *name, char value);

functions.signature: size_t ippFileExpandVars(ipp_file_t *file, char *dst, const char *src, size_t dstsize);
functions.description: Expands ${var} references in src using variables defined in the ipp_file_t context into dst, up to dstsize bytes. Returns the number of bytes that would be/were written.
requirements: file must be valid.
src must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
dst may be NULL to query required length; if non-NULL it must reference at least dstsize bytes.
dstsize should be sufficient to hold expanded output including NUL.

functions.name: ippFileGetAttribute
functions.description: Retrieves a parsed attribute by name and expected value tag from an IPP data file parsing context.
requirements: file must be valid.
name must be non-NULL.
value_tag should match the expected attribute value type.

functions.name: ippFileGetAttributes
functions.description: Returns the current set of parsed attributes as an IPP collection from the file parsing context.
requirements: file must be valid.

functions.name: ippFileGetFilename
functions.description: Returns the filename associated with the ipp_file_t, if any.
requirements: file must be valid.

functions.name: ippFileGetLineNumber
functions.description: Returns the current line number in the file being parsed or written by the ipp_file_t.
requirements: file must be valid.

functions.name: ippFileGetVar
functions.description: Retrieves the value of a named variable from the ipp_file_t's variable map.
requirements: file must be valid.
name must be non-NULL.

functions.name: ippFileNew
functions.signature: ipp_file_t *ippFileNew(ipp_file_t *parent, ipp_fattr_cb_t attr_cb, ipp_ferror_cb_t error_cb, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Creates a new IPP data file context, optionally inheriting settings from parent and using provided callbacks for attributes, errors, and user data.
requirements: parent may be NULL or a valid ipp_file_t to inherit context.
attr_cb, error_cb may be NULL or function pointers of the specified types.
cb_data is an opaque pointer passed to callbacks.

functions.name: ippFileOpen
functions.signature: bool ippFileOpen(ipp_file_t *file, const char *filename, const char *mode);
functions.description: Opens a file on disk for reading/writing within an existing ipp_file_t context, using fopen-style mode.
requirements: file must be a valid ipp_file_t created by ippFileNew.
filename must be non-NULL.
mode must be a valid fopen-style mode string (e.g., "r", "w").

functions.name: ippFileRead
functions.signature: bool ippFileRead(ipp_file_t *file, ipp_ftoken_cb_t token_cb, bool with_groups);
functions.description: Parses an IPP data file, invoking token_cb for each token; when with_groups is true, includes group tag tokens.
requirements: file must be valid and opened for reading.
token_cb must be a valid callback function; it may be invoked multiple times.
with_groups selects whether group tokens are emitted.

functions.name: ippFileReadCollection
functions.description: Reads and returns a single collection (attribute set) from the IPP data file stream.
requirements: file must be valid and positioned at a collection in the input.

functions.name: ippFileReadToken
functions.description: Reads the next token from the IPP data file into token buffer, up to tokensize bytes including NUL.
requirements: file must be valid and opened for reading.
token must be non-NULL and have capacity of at least tokensize.
tokensize must be > 0.

functions.name: ippFileRestorePosition
functions.description: Restores the file stream position to the last saved position for the ipp_file_t.
requirements: file must be valid.
A position must have been previously saved with ippFileSavePosition.

functions.name: ippFileSavePosition
functions.description: Saves the current file stream position for later restoration.
requirements: file must be valid.

functions.name: ippFileSetAttributes
functions.description: Associates a set of attributes (as an IPP object) with the file context for writing.
requirements: file must be valid.
attrs must be a valid ipp_t pointer representing attributes.

functions.name: ippFileSetGroupTag
functions.description: Sets the current group tag for subsequently written attributes in the file context.
requirements: file must be valid.
group_tag must be a valid group tag (e.g., IPP_TAG_OPERATION, IPP_TAG_JOB, etc.).

functions.name: ippFileSetVar
functions.signature: bool ippFileSetVar(ipp_file_t *file, const char *name, const char *value);
functions.description: Sets or updates a variable in the file context's variable map.
requirements: file must be valid.
name must be non-NULL.
value must be non-NULL.

functions.name: ippFileSetVarf
functions.signature: bool ippFileSetVarf(ipp_file_t *file, const char *name, const char *value, ...);
functions.description: Formats and sets a variable value using printf-style arguments for the given variable name in the file context.
requirements: file must be valid.
name must be non-NULL.
value must be a non-NULL printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match the format.

functions.name: ippFileWriteAttributes
functions.description: Writes the attributes from the given IPP object to the file in a textual form; when with_groups is true, includes group markers.
requirements: file must be valid and opened for writing.
ipp must be a valid IPP object.
with_groups selects whether group tags are included.

functions.name: ippFileWriteComment
functions.description: Writes a formatted comment line to the IPP data file.
requirements: file must be valid and opened for writing.
comment must be a non-NULL printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match the format.

functions.name: ippFileWriteToken
functions.description: Writes a literal token to the IPP data file.
requirements: file must be valid and opened for writing.
token must be non-NULL.

functions.name: ippFileWriteTokenf
functions.description: Writes a formatted token to the IPP data file using printf-style formatting.
requirements: file must be valid and opened for writing.
token must be a non-NULL printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match the format.

functions.name: ippFindAttribute
functions.description: Finds the first attribute with the specified name (and optionally value type) in the IPP message and returns it.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
name must be non-NULL.
value_tag may be IPP_TAG_ZERO or a specific expected tag; when non-zero it should match the attribute's type for a positive match.

functions.name: ippFindNextAttribute
functions.description: Continues searching for the next attribute matching name (and optionally tag) starting after the current iterator position.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
name must be non-NULL.
Typically used after ippFindAttribute or iterators to continue searching.

functions.name: ippFirstAttribute
functions.description: Deprecated: Use ippGetFirstAttribute instead. Returns the first attribute in the IPP message and sets iteration state.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
Prefer ippGetFirstAttribute for new code.

functions.name: ippGetBoolean
functions.description: Returns the boolean value at the given index from a boolean attribute, as an int (0 or 1).
requirements: attr must be valid and boolean-compatible.
element must be within [0, ippGetCount(attr)).

functions.name: ippGetCollection
functions.description: Returns the collection value at the given index from a collection attribute.
requirements: attr must be valid and contain collection values.
element must be within range of existing values.

functions.name: ippGetCount
functions.description: Returns the number of values contained in the attribute.
requirements: attr must be valid.

functions.name: ippGetDate
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the dateTime value at the given index from a date attribute.
requirements: attr must be valid and contain dateTime values.
element must be within range.

functions.name: ippGetFirstAttribute
functions.description: Returns the first attribute in the IPP message and initializes internal iteration state for subsequent ippGetNextAttribute calls.
requirements: ipp must be valid.

functions.name: ippGetGroupTag
functions.description: Returns the group tag (e.g., operation, job) associated with the attribute.
requirements: attr must be valid.

functions.name: ippGetInteger
functions.description: Returns the integer value at the given index from an integer or enum attribute.
requirements: attr must be valid and integer-compatible (IPP_TAG_INTEGER or IPP_TAG_ENUM).
element must be within range.

functions.name: ippGetLength
functions.description: Returns the current length in bytes of the IPP message when encoded (or an estimate suitable for buffer sizing).
requirements: ipp must be valid.

functions.name: ippGetName
functions.description: Returns the attribute's name string.
requirements: attr must be valid.

functions.name: ippGetNextAttribute
functions.description: Returns the next attribute in the IPP message following the last retrieved by ippGetFirstAttribute/ippGetNextAttribute.
requirements: ipp must be valid and iteration should have been initialized (e.g., via ippGetFirstAttribute).

functions.name: ippGetOctetString
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the octetString data buffer at the given index and sets datalen to its length if non-NULL.
requirements: attr must be valid and contain octetString values.
element must be within range.
datalen may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a valid pointer to receive the length.

functions.name: ippGetOperation
functions.description: Returns the IPP operation code set in the request/response header of the message.
requirements: ipp must be valid.

functions.name: ippGetPort
functions.description: Returns the default IPP TCP port number currently configured (typically 631).

functions.name: ippGetRange
functions.description: Returns the lower bound of the rangeOfInteger at the given index and stores the upper bound to *upper if non-NULL.
requirements: attr must be valid and contain rangeOfInteger values.
element must be within range.
upper may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: ippGetRequestId
functions.description: Returns the request-id from the IPP message header.
requirements: ipp must be valid.

functions.name: ippGetResolution
functions.signature: int ippGetResolution(ipp_attribute_t *attr, int element, int *yres, ipp_res_t *units);
functions.description: Returns the X resolution at the given index and stores the Y resolution and units via yres and units if non-NULL.
requirements: attr must be valid and contain resolution values.
element must be within range.
yres and units may be NULL; if non-NULL they must be valid pointers.

functions.name: ippGetState
functions.description: Returns the current read/write state of the IPP message object.
requirements: ipp must be valid.

functions.name: ippGetStatusCode
functions.description: Returns the IPP status code from a response message.
requirements: ipp must be valid.

functions.name: ippGetString
functions.signature: const char *ippGetString(ipp_attribute_t *attr, int element, const char **language);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the string value at the given index and stores the associated language tag pointer (if any) through language.
requirements: attr must be valid and contain string values.
element must be within range.
language may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a valid pointer to receive a language tag pointer or NULL.

functions.name: ippGetValueTag
functions.description: Returns the value tag (type) of the attribute (e.g., integer, name, boolean).
requirements: attr must be valid.

functions.name: ippGetVersion
functions.description: Returns the major version of the IPP message and stores the minor version via minor if non-NULL.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
minor may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: ippLength
functions.description: Deprecated: Use ippGetLength instead. Returns the encoded length of the IPP message.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
Prefer ippGetLength for new code.

functions.name: ippNew
functions.description: Creates a new empty IPP message object with default header values.

functions.name: ippNewRequest
functions.description: Creates a new IPP request message with the given operation code set in the header.
requirements: op must be a valid IPP operation code.

functions.name: ippNewResponse
functions.description: Creates a new IPP response message initialized from a request (e.g., matching version, request-id).
requirements: request must be a valid IPP request object.

functions.name: ippNextAttribute
functions.description: Deprecated: Use ippGetNextAttribute instead. Returns the next attribute in the iteration sequence.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
Prefer ippGetNextAttribute for new code.

functions.name: ippOpString
functions.description: Returns the standard operation name string for the given IPP operation code.
requirements: op should be a valid IPP operation code.

functions.name: ippOpValue
functions.description: Parses and returns the IPP operation code corresponding to the provided operation name string.
requirements: name must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.

functions.name: ippPort
functions.description: Deprecated: Use ippGetPort instead. Returns the default IPP TCP port number.
requirements: Prefer ippGetPort for new code.

functions.name: ippRead
functions.description: Reads IPP data from the given HTTP connection into the IPP object, advancing its state machine.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection handle.
ipp must be a valid IPP object prepared to receive data.

functions.name: ippReadFile
functions.description: Reads IPP data from a file descriptor into the IPP object.
requirements: fd must be a valid readable file descriptor.
ipp must be a valid IPP object.

functions.name: ippReadIO
functions.signature: ipp_state_t ippReadIO(void *src, ipp_io_cb_t cb, int blocking, ipp_t *parent, ipp_t *ipp);
functions.description: Reads IPP data using a caller-supplied I/O callback. The callback pulls bytes from src; blocking selects blocking vs non-blocking behavior; parent may link the read IPP into a larger message context.
requirements: cb must be a valid function matching ipp_io_cb_t that reads up to 'bytes' into buffer and returns the number of bytes read or <0 on error.
src is passed to cb as its context and must be valid for cb.
ipp must be a valid IPP object.
blocking is typically 0/1 for non-blocking/blocking reads.
parent may be NULL or a valid IPP object.

functions.name: ippRestore
functions.description: Restores the IPP object's internal state (e.g., after ippSave).
requirements: ipp must be valid.
ippSave should have been called previously to create a saved state.

functions.name: ippSave
functions.description: Saves the IPP object's current internal state for later restoration via ippRestore.
requirements: ipp must be valid.

functions.name: ippSetBoolean
functions.signature: int ippSetBoolean(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, int element, int boolvalue);
functions.description: Sets or replaces the boolean value at the specified index of an attribute in an IPP message, possibly creating it if needed.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must be non-NULL and point to an attribute pointer owned by ipp (may be NULL to create depending on implementation).
element must be >= 0 and within or at the next index as allowed by the library.
boolvalue will be interpreted as 0/1.

functions.name: ippSetCollection
functions.signature: int ippSetCollection(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, int element, ipp_t *colvalue);
functions.description: Sets the collection value at the given index of an attribute to colvalue.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference a collection attribute pointer owned by ipp.
element must be >= 0 and within range.
colvalue must be a valid ipp_t collection.

functions.name: ippSetDate
functions.signature: int ippSetDate(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, int element, const ipp_uchar_t *datevalue);
functions.description: Sets the dateTime value at the given index of an attribute from the provided IPP date byte array.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference a date attribute pointer owned by ipp.
element must be >= 0 and within range.
datevalue must point to a valid IPP date/time array.

functions.name: ippSetGroupTag
functions.description: Changes the group tag associated with an existing attribute in an IPP message.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must be non-NULL and reference an attribute belonging to ipp.
group_tag must be a valid group tag.

functions.name: ippSetInteger
functions.signature: int ippSetInteger(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, int element, int intvalue);
functions.description: Sets the integer value at the given index of an integer/enum attribute.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference an integer-compatible attribute owned by ipp.
element must be >= 0 and within range.

functions.name: ippSetName
functions.description: Renames an attribute in the IPP message to the given name.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference an attribute belonging to ipp.
name must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.

functions.name: ippSetOctetString
functions.signature: int ippSetOctetString(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, int element, const void *data, int datalen);
functions.description: Sets the octetString value at the given index using data of length datalen.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference an octetString attribute owned by ipp.
element must be >= 0 and within range.
If datalen > 0, data must be non-NULL and at least datalen bytes long.
datalen must be >= 0.

functions.name: ippSetOperation
functions.description: Sets the IPP operation code in the message header.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
op must be a valid IPP operation code.

functions.name: ippSetPort
functions.description: Sets the process-wide default IPP TCP port number to p.
requirements: p should be a valid TCP port number (1–65535).
Affects subsequent default port queries (ippGetPort/ippPort).

functions.name: ippSetRange
functions.signature: int ippSetRange(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, int element, int lowervalue, int uppervalue);
functions.description: Sets the rangeOfInteger value at the given index to the inclusive bounds [lowervalue, uppervalue].
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference a rangeOfInteger attribute owned by ipp.
element must be >= 0 and within range.
Typically lowervalue <= uppervalue.

functions.name: ippSetRequestId
functions.description: Sets the request-id field in the IPP message header.
requirements: ipp must be valid.

functions.name: ippSetResolution
functions.signature: int ippSetResolution(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, int element, ipp_res_t unitsvalue, int xresvalue, int yresvalue);
functions.description: Sets the resolution value at the given index to the specified units and X/Y resolutions.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference a resolution attribute owned by ipp.
element must be >= 0 and within range.
unitsvalue must be IPP_RES_PER_INCH or IPP_RES_PER_CM.
xresvalue and yresvalue should be positive integers.

functions.name: ippSetState
functions.description: Sets the internal state of the IPP object’s read/write state machine.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
state must be a valid ipp_state_t value.

functions.name: ippSetStatusCode
functions.description: Sets the IPP status code in a response message header.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
status must be a valid ipp_status_t.

functions.name: ippSetString
functions.signature: int ippSetString(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, int element, const char *strvalue);
functions.description: Sets the string value at the given index of a string attribute to strvalue.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference a string-compatible attribute owned by ipp.
element must be >= 0 and within range.
strvalue must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.

functions.name: ippSetStringf
functions.signature: int ippSetStringf(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, int element, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Formats a string using printf-style arguments and sets it as the value at the given index of a string attribute.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference a string-compatible attribute owned by ipp.
element must be >= 0 and within range.
format must be a non-NULL printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match the format.

functions.name: ippSetStringfv
functions.signature: int ippSetStringfv(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, int element, const char *format, va_list ap);
functions.description: Formats a string using a va_list and sets it as the value at the given index of a string attribute.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference a string-compatible attribute owned by ipp.
element must be >= 0 and within range.
format must be non-NULL; ap must be an initialized va_list matching the format.

functions.name: ippSetValueTag
functions.description: Changes the value tag (type) of an existing attribute in the IPP message.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference an attribute owned by ipp.
value_tag must be a valid value tag appropriate for the attribute's data.

functions.name: ippSetVersion
functions.signature: int ippSetVersion(ipp_t *ipp, int major, int minor);
functions.description: Sets the IPP protocol version (major.minor) in the message header.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
major and minor should be non-negative and represent a supported IPP version.

functions.name: ippStateString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing the IPP object state value.
requirements: state must be a valid ipp_state_t value.

functions.name: ippTagString
functions.description: Returns the canonical name string for the given IPP tag value.
requirements: tag must be a valid ipp_tag_t.

functions.name: ippTagValue
functions.description: Parses and returns the IPP tag value corresponding to the provided tag name string.
requirements: name must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.

functions.name: ippTimeToDate
functions.description: Converts a time_t value to an IPP dateTime byte array (typically 11 bytes) and returns a pointer to it.
requirements: t is a time value; returned pointer is valid until the next call or per implementation notes (lifetime unspecified here).

functions.name: ippValidateAttribute
functions.description: Validates a single attribute’s syntax and value(s) according to IPP rules. Returns non-zero if valid.
requirements: attr must be valid.

functions.name: ippValidateAttributes
functions.description: Validates all attributes in an IPP message for correctness and conformance. Returns non-zero if valid.
requirements: ipp must be valid.

functions.name: ippWrite
functions.description: Writes (encodes and sends) IPP data for the message over the given HTTP connection, advancing its state machine.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connected to the destination.
ipp must be a valid IPP object ready to be written.

functions.name: ippWriteFile
functions.description: Writes the IPP message to a file descriptor.
requirements: fd must be a valid writable file descriptor.
ipp must be a valid IPP object.

functions.name: ippWriteIO
functions.signature: ipp_state_t ippWriteIO(void *dst, ipp_io_cb_t cb, int blocking, ipp_t *parent, ipp_t *ipp);
functions.description: Writes IPP data using a caller-supplied I/O callback. The callback is invoked to write bytes to dst; blocking selects blocking behavior; parent may link in a larger context.
requirements: cb must be a valid function matching ipp_io_cb_t that writes up to 'bytes' from buffer and returns the number of bytes written or <0 on error.
dst is passed to cb as its context and must be valid for cb.
ipp must be a valid IPP object.
blocking is typically 0/1 for non-blocking/blocking writes.
parent may be NULL or a valid IPP object.

functions.name: pwgFormatSizeName
functions.signature: extern int pwgFormatSizeName(char *keyword, size_t keysize, const char *prefix, const char *name, int width, int length, const char *units) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Formats a PWG 5101.1-compliant media size keyword string into the provided buffer based on the given parts (optional prefix, base name, size and units). Useful for generating media keywords that include a vendor or family prefix and a size descriptor. Details such as the exact format and accepted unit strings are not documented here and remain unknown.
requirements: keyword must point to a writable buffer with at least keysize bytes.
keysize must be greater than 0 to allow writing a NUL-terminated keyword.

width and length are integers representing the media dimensions; the valid range and units are not explicitly documented here (units is provided separately); values should represent a real, non-zero media size.
prefix, name, and units must be valid NUL-terminated strings; accepted values and whether prefix may be NULL are not documented here (unknown).
The function returns an int status; callers must check the return value for success/failure (exact semantics of the return value are not documented here and are unknown).

functions.name: pwgInitSize
functions.description: Initializes a pwg_size_t structure using information from IPP attributes in the provided job object, and reports whether margins were set. Intended to populate size dimensions and margins consistent with the job's requested media.
requirements: size must be a non-NULL pointer to a pwg_size_t structure that the function can write to.
margins_set must be a non-NULL pointer to an int for output; it will be set to indicate whether margin values were determined (exact value convention is not documented here and is unknown).
job must be a valid ipp_t pointer containing the relevant IPP attributes; whether NULL is allowed is not documented (unknown).
The function returns an int status; callers must check the return value for success/failure (exact semantics of the return value are not documented here and are unknown).
Any pwg_size_t fields written are in 2540ths (hundredths of millimeters, per the surrounding type documentation); callers must interpret the resulting fields using that unit.

functions.name: pwgMediaForLegacy
functions.description: Looks up media size information by an IPP/ISO legacy media name and returns a pointer to a pwg_media_t describing the media (names and dimensions). Use to translate a legacy media keyword to the standardized PWG entry.
requirements: legacy must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing a legacy media name.
Return value may be NULL if the media is not found; callers must check for NULL before use (exact not-found behavior is not documented but NULL is the conventional C pattern).
Ownership and mutability of the returned pwg_media_t are not documented (unknown); callers should not assume they can free or modify it.

functions.name: pwgMediaForPPD
functions.description: Looks up media size information by an Adobe PPD media name and returns a pointer to a pwg_media_t describing the media. Use to translate a PPD media keyword to the standardized PWG entry.
requirements: ppd must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing a PPD media name.
Return value may be NULL if the media is not found; callers must check for NULL before use (exact not-found behavior is not documented but NULL is the conventional C pattern).
Ownership and mutability of the returned pwg_media_t are not documented (unknown); callers should not assume they can free or modify it.

functions.name: pwgMediaForPWG
functions.description: Looks up media size information by a PWG 5101.1 self-describing media keyword and returns a pointer to a pwg_media_t describing the media. Use to resolve a PWG media keyword to standardized dimensions and aliases.
requirements: pwg must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing a PWG media keyword.
Return value may be NULL if the media is not found; callers must check for NULL before use (exact not-found behavior is not documented but NULL is the conventional C pattern).
Ownership and mutability of the returned pwg_media_t are not documented (unknown); callers should not assume they can free or modify it.

functions.name: pwgMediaForSize
functions.description: Looks up media size information by physical dimensions and returns a pointer to a pwg_media_t describing the closest matching media. Use when you have dimensions and need the corresponding standardized PWG entry.
requirements: width and length are integers representing media dimensions in 2540ths (hundredths of millimeters), consistent with the surrounding type documentation; values should represent a real, non-zero media size.
Return value may be NULL if no matching media is found; callers must check for NULL before use (exact matching behavior is not documented here and is unknown).
Ownership and mutability of the returned pwg_media_t are not documented (unknown); callers should not assume they can free or modify it.
Use PWG_FROM_POINTS/PWG_TO_POINTS to convert between points and 2540ths when preparing inputs or interpreting results.

functions.name: httpAcceptConnection
functions.description: Accept a new HTTP connection on an existing listening socket. Returns a new http_t handle for the connection. The blocking parameter controls blocking/non-blocking mode on the accepted socket.
requirements: fd must be a valid listening socket descriptor.
blocking must be either 0 (non-blocking) or non-zero (blocking).
Caller must close the returned connection with httpClose when finished.

functions.name: httpAddCredential
functions.signature: int httpAddCredential(cups_array_t *credentials, const void *data, size_t datalen);
functions.description: DEPRECATED. Add a credential blob to a credentials array. Use newer credentials APIs instead.
requirements: credentials must be a valid cups_array_t pointer capable of storing credential blobs.
data must point to a buffer of length datalen.
datalen must match the size of the credential data.

functions.name: httpAddrAny
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpAddrIsAny). Test whether the supplied address is the "any"/wildcard address.
requirements: addr must not be NULL.

functions.name: httpAddrClose
functions.description: Close a TCP/UDP socket associated with addr. Primarily a convenience around close/shutdown with address context.
requirements: addr must not be NULL.
fd must be a valid open socket descriptor.

functions.name: httpAddrConnect
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpAddrConnect2). Attempt to connect to one of the addresses in addrlist. On success returns the address used and stores the socket in *sock.
requirements: addrlist must reference at least one valid address.
sock must not be NULL and will receive the connected socket descriptor.

functions.name: httpAddrConnect2
functions.description: Connect to one of the addresses in addrlist with an optional timeout and cancellation. Returns the address used and sets *sock to the connected socket.
requirements: addrlist must reference at least one valid address.
sock must not be NULL and will receive the connected socket descriptor.
msec is the timeout in milliseconds; non-negative values imply a timeout, 0 may mean immediate/none (exact semantics unknown).
If cancel is non-NULL, the pointed-to value may be polled to cancel the attempt (exact nonzero/zero semantics unknown).

functions.name: httpAddrCopyList
functions.description: Create a deep copy of an address list.
requirements: src must be either NULL or a valid address list.
Caller must free the returned list with httpAddrFreeList.

functions.name: httpAddrEqual
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpAddrIsEqual). Compare two addresses for equality.
requirements: addr1 and addr2 must not be NULL.

functions.name: httpAddrFamily
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpAddrGetFamily). Return the address family (e.g., AF_INET/AF_INET6/AF_LOCAL).
requirements: addr must not be NULL.

functions.name: httpAddrFreeList
functions.description: Free an address list allocated by CUPS address APIs.
requirements: addrlist must be either NULL or a list previously allocated by CUPS (e.g., httpAddrGetList, httpAddrCopyList).
Do not use addrlist after calling this function.

functions.name: httpAddrGetFamily
functions.description: Return the address family (AF_*) of the given address.
requirements: addr must not be NULL.

functions.name: httpAddrGetLength
functions.description: Return the length in bytes of the socket address stored in addr (e.g., sizeof(sockaddr_in/6/un)).
requirements: addr must not be NULL.

functions.name: httpAddrGetList
functions.signature: http_addrlist_t *httpAddrGetList(const char *hostname, int family, const char *service);
functions.description: Resolve a hostname and optional service to a list of socket addresses.
requirements: hostname must be a valid host name or address string.
family should be an address family hint (e.g., AF_UNSPEC/AF_INET/AF_INET6).
service may be NULL or a service/port string.
Caller must free the returned list with httpAddrFreeList.

functions.name: httpAddrGetPort
functions.description: Return the TCP/UDP port number stored in addr.
requirements: addr must not be NULL.

functions.name: httpAddrGetString
functions.description: Format addr as a human-readable string into s.
requirements: addr must not be NULL.
s must point to a writable buffer of at least slen bytes.
slen must be greater than 0 to store any characters.

functions.name: httpAddrIsAny
functions.description: Return whether addr is an "any"/wildcard address.
requirements: addr must not be NULL.

functions.name: httpAddrIsEqual
functions.description: Return whether two addresses are equal (same family and value).
requirements: addr1 and addr2 must not be NULL.

functions.name: httpAddrIsLocalhost
functions.description: Return whether addr refers to localhost/loopback.
requirements: addr must not be NULL.

functions.name: httpAddrLength
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpAddrGetLength). Return the length of the socket address in bytes.
requirements: addr must not be NULL.

functions.name: httpAddrListen
functions.description: Create and listen on a server socket bound to addr:port.
requirements: addr must not be NULL and must contain a bindable address.
port must be a valid TCP port number (typically 0-65535).

functions.name: httpAddrLocalhost
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpAddrIsLocalhost). Test whether addr is localhost.
requirements: addr must not be NULL.

functions.name: httpAddrLookup
functions.description: Lookup the hostname for addr and write it to name.
requirements: addr must not be NULL.
name must point to a writable buffer of at least namelen bytes.
namelen must be greater than 0 to store any characters.

functions.name: httpAddrSetPort
functions.description: Set the port in the socket address.
requirements: addr must not be NULL.
port must be a valid port number (typically 0-65535).

functions.name: httpAddrString
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpAddrGetString). Format addr as a string into s.
requirements: addr must not be NULL.
s must point to a writable buffer of at least slen bytes.
slen must be greater than 0 to store any characters.

functions.name: httpAddrPort
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpAddrGetPort). Return the port number from addr.
requirements: addr must not be NULL.

functions.name: httpAssembleURI
functions.signature: http_uri_status_t httpAssembleURI(http_uri_coding_t encoding, char *uri, int urilen, const char *scheme, const char *username, const char *host, int port, const char *resource);
functions.description: Assemble a URI string from components, optionally encoding parts as specified.
requirements: uri must point to a writable buffer of at least urilen bytes.
urilen must be large enough to hold the full URI including NUL; otherwise HTTP_URI_STATUS_OVERFLOW is returned.
encoding controls which URI parts are encoded; choose values from http_uri_coding_t.
scheme, username, host, resource may be NULL depending on the scheme; semantics for NULL/empty components are implementation-defined.
port must be a valid port number or 0/-1 to omit (exact sentinel unknown).

functions.name: httpAssembleURIf
functions.signature: http_uri_status_t httpAssembleURIf(http_uri_coding_t encoding, char *uri, int urilen, const char *scheme, const char *username, const char *host, int port, const char *resourcef, ...);
functions.description: Assemble a URI string using a printf-style resource format string and varargs, optionally encoding parts as specified.
requirements: uri must point to a writable buffer of at least urilen bytes.
urilen must be sufficient for the full formatted URI including NUL.
resourcef must be a valid printf-style format string for the resource component with corresponding varargs.
Other component requirements are the same as httpAssembleURI.

functions.name: httpAssembleUUID
functions.signature: char *httpAssembleUUID(const char *server, int port, const char *name, int number, char *buffer, size_t bufsize);
functions.description: Assemble a CUPS-style UUID string using server, port, name, and number, writing it into buffer.
requirements: buffer must point to a writable buffer of at least bufsize bytes.
bufsize must be large enough to hold the UUID including NUL.
server and name are strings used to form the UUID; may not be NULL if required by format (exact rules unknown).
port and number are integers incorporated into the UUID.

functions.name: httpBlocking
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpSetBlocking). Set blocking/non-blocking mode on an HTTP connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
b must be 0 (non-blocking) or non-zero (blocking).

functions.name: httpCheck
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpWait). Check whether data is available or the connection is ready (exact semantics unknown).
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpClearCookie
functions.description: Clear any Cookie header/value associated with the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpClearFields
functions.description: Clear all request header fields for the connection so a fresh request can be composed.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpClose
functions.description: Close and free an HTTP connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection or NULL.
Connection should not be used after closing.

functions.name: httpCompareCredentials
functions.description: DEPRECATED. Compare two credential arrays for equivalence.
requirements: cred1 and cred2 must be valid credential arrays.

functions.name: httpConnect
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpConnect2). Open a new HTTP connection to host:port.
requirements: host must be a valid hostname or address string.
port must be a valid TCP port number.
Caller must close the returned connection with httpClose.

functions.name: httpConnect2
functions.signature: http_t *httpConnect2(const char *host, int port, http_addrlist_t *addrlist, int family, http_encryption_t encryption, int blocking, int msec, int *cancel);
functions.description: Open a new HTTP connection to host:port using optional address list, family hint, encryption policy, blocking mode, timeout, and cancellation.
requirements: host must be a valid hostname or address.
port must be a valid TCP port number.
If addrlist is provided, it must be a valid list produced by CUPS address APIs.
family is an address family hint (e.g., AF_UNSPEC/AF_INET/AF_INET6).
encryption must be a valid http_encryption_t value.
blocking must be 0 (non-blocking) or non-zero (blocking).
msec is a timeout in milliseconds (exact semantics for 0/negative unknown).
If cancel is non-NULL, it points to a flag polled for cancellation (non-zero/zero semantics unknown).
Caller must close the returned connection with httpClose.

functions.name: httpConnectAgain
functions.description: Attempt to re-establish a previously failed or closed connection, with optional timeout and cancellation.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection object.
msec is a timeout in milliseconds (exact semantics unknown).
If cancel is non-NULL, it points to a cancellation flag (semantics unknown).

functions.name: httpConnectEncrypt
functions.signature: http_t *httpConnectEncrypt(const char *host, int port, http_encryption_t encryption);
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpConnect2). Open a new HTTP connection to host:port with specified encryption policy.
requirements: host must be a valid hostname or address string.
port must be a valid TCP port number.
encryption must be a valid http_encryption_t value.
Caller must close the returned connection with httpClose.

functions.name: httpConnectURI
functions.signature: http_t *httpConnectURI(const char *uri, char *host, size_t hsize, int *port, char *resource, size_t rsize, bool blocking, int msec, int *cancel, bool require_ca);
functions.description: Open a new connection based on a URI string, optionally returning parsed host/port/resource and controlling blocking, timeout, cancellation, and CA requirement.
requirements: uri must be a valid URI string.
If host is non-NULL, it must point to a buffer of at least hsize bytes to receive the hostname.
If port is non-NULL, it will receive the parsed port.
If resource is non-NULL, it must point to a buffer of at least rsize bytes to receive the resource path.
blocking selects blocking or non-blocking mode.
msec is a timeout in milliseconds (exact semantics unknown).
If cancel is non-NULL, it points to a cancellation flag (semantics unknown).
If require_ca is true, a valid CA must be available for secure connections (policy semantics not detailed).
Caller must close the returned connection with httpClose.

functions.name: httpCopyCredentials
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpCopyPeerCredentials). Copy peer credentials from an HTTP connection into a credentials array.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
credentials must not be NULL; on success it will point to an allocated array the caller must eventually free (API-dependent).

functions.name: httpCopyPeerCredentials
functions.description: Return a newly-allocated string describing the peer credentials for the current connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
Caller must free the returned string with free().

functions.name: httpCredentialsAreValidForName
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use cupsAreCredentialsValidForName). Validate whether credentials are valid for the specified common name.
requirements: credentials must be a valid credential array.
common_name must be a non-NULL string.

functions.name: httpCredentialsGetExpiration
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use cupsGetCredentialsExpiration). Return the expiration time associated with the credentials.
requirements: credentials must be a valid credential array.

functions.name: httpCredentialsGetTrust
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use cupsGetCredentialsTrust). Determine the trust level of credentials for a given common name.
requirements: credentials must be a valid credential array.
common_name must be a non-NULL string.

functions.name: httpCredentialsString
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use cupsGetCredentialsInfo). Format credential information as text into buffer.
requirements: credentials must be a valid credential array.
buffer must point to a writable buffer of at least bufsize bytes.
bufsize must be greater than 0 to store any characters.

functions.name: httpDecode64
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpDecode64_3). Decode Base64 text from in into out.
requirements: out must point to a writable buffer sufficiently large for the decoded data (size not provided; use httpDecode64_3 instead).
in must be a NUL-terminated Base64 string.

functions.name: httpDecode64_2
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpDecode64_3). Decode Base64 from in into out, writing the decoded length to *outlen.
requirements: out must point to a writable buffer large enough for decoded data.
outlen must not be NULL; on success it receives the number of decoded bytes.
in must be a NUL-terminated Base64 string.

functions.name: httpDecode64_3
functions.signature: char *httpDecode64_3(char *out, size_t *outlen, const char *in, const char **end);
functions.description: Decode Base64 text from in into out. Writes the number of bytes decoded to *outlen and, if end is non-NULL, stores a pointer to the character after the last processed byte.
requirements: out must point to a writable buffer large enough for decoded data (caller must ensure capacity).
outlen must not be NULL and will receive the number of decoded bytes written to out.
in must be a NUL-terminated string containing Base64 data.
If end is non-NULL, it will receive a pointer into in just after the decoded segment.

functions.name: httpDelete
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpWriteRequest). Send an HTTP DELETE request for the given URI.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
uri must be a valid, properly formatted path or absolute URI depending on server expectations.

functions.name: httpEncode64
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpEncode64_2). Encode a NUL-terminated input buffer in Base64 and write to out.
requirements: out must point to a writable buffer large enough for the Base64-encoded output including NUL terminator.
in must be a NUL-terminated string of data to encode.

functions.name: httpEncode64_2
functions.signature: char *httpEncode64_2(char *out, int outlen, const char *in, int inlen);
functions.description: Encode binary input data to Base64 and write into out, which is outlen bytes long.
requirements: out must point to a writable buffer of at least outlen bytes.
outlen must be large enough to hold the Base64-encoded data including NUL terminator.
in must point to inlen bytes of data to encode.

functions.name: httpEncode64_3
functions.signature: char *httpEncode64_3(char *out, size_t outlen, const char *in, size_t inlen, bool url);
functions.description: Encode binary input data to Base64 (or URL-safe Base64 when url is true) and write into out.
requirements: out must point to a writable buffer of at least outlen bytes.
outlen must be large enough to hold the encoded data including NUL terminator.
in must point to inlen bytes of data to encode.
url selects URL-safe Base64 alphabet when true.

functions.name: httpEncryption
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpSetEncryption). Set the encryption policy for an HTTP connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
e must be one of http_encryption_t values.

functions.name: httpError
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpGetError). Return the last error code/state for the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpFieldValue
functions.description: Map an HTTP header field name to its http_field_t enumeration value.
requirements: name must be a NUL-terminated header field name string.

functions.name: httpFlush
functions.description: Flush any pending read data from the connection (or ensure output/input state is clean).
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpFlushWrite
functions.description: Flush any buffered write data to the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpFreeCredentials
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use free). Free a credentials array structure.
requirements: certs must be a credentials array allocated by the older credentials APIs.
Do not use certs after freeing.

functions.name: httpGet
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpWriteRequest). Send an HTTP GET request for the given URI.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
uri must be a valid request-target/path or absolute URI as required.

functions.name: httpGetActivity
functions.description: Return the last activity time on the HTTP connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGetAddress
functions.description: Return a pointer to the peer/local socket address associated with the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
Returned pointer refers to memory owned by the connection; do not free.

functions.name: httpGetAuthString
functions.description: Return the current Authorization header string for the connection, if any.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
Returned pointer semantics (owned vs. allocated) are not specified here; treat as read-only.

functions.name: httpGetBlocking
functions.description: Return whether the connection is set to blocking (non-zero) or non-blocking (0).
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGetContentEncoding
functions.description: Return the current Content-Encoding header value for the response or request in context.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
Returned string is owned by the connection; do not modify or free.

functions.name: httpGetCookie
functions.description: Return the current Cookie header value for the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
Returned string is owned by the connection; do not modify or free.

functions.name: httpGetCookieValue
functions.signature: char *httpGetCookieValue(http_t *http, const char *name, char *buffer, size_t bufsize);
functions.description: Extract the value of a named cookie from the connection and write it into buffer.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
name must be a NUL-terminated cookie name.
buffer must point to a writable buffer of at least bufsize bytes.
bufsize must be greater than 0 to store any characters.

functions.name: httpGetDateString
functions.description: Return a static string containing an HTTP-formatted date for time t.
requirements: t is a time_t value.

functions.name: httpGetDateString2
functions.signature: const char *httpGetDateString2(time_t t, char *s, int slen);
functions.description: Format an HTTP date for time t into the supplied buffer and return s.
requirements: s must point to a writable buffer of at least slen bytes.
slen must be large enough to hold the formatted date including NUL.

functions.name: httpGetDateTime
functions.description: Parse an HTTP-formatted date/time string and return the corresponding time_t.
requirements: s must be a NUL-terminated date/time string in an HTTP-supported format.

functions.name: httpGetEncryption
functions.description: Return the current encryption setting/state for the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGetError
functions.description: Return the last error code/state for the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGetExpect
functions.description: Return the current Expect/response status state for the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGetFd
functions.description: Return the underlying socket file descriptor for the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGetField
functions.description: Return the value of the specified HTTP header field for the current request/response.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
field must be a valid http_field_t value.
Returned string is owned by the connection; do not modify or free.

functions.name: httpGetHostByName
functions.description: Perform a hostname lookup and return a hostent structure.
requirements: name must be a NUL-terminated hostname or address string.
Returned pointer may refer to static storage; treat accordingly.

functions.name: httpGetHostname
functions.description: Return the hostname associated with the connection, optionally writing it into s.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
If s is non-NULL, it must point to a buffer of at least slen bytes.
Returned string may be owned by the connection or s if provided; do not free owned strings.

functions.name: httpGetKeepAlive
functions.description: Return the current keep-alive setting for the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGetLength
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpGetLength2). Return the Content-Length of the current message, if known.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGetLength2
functions.description: Return the Content-Length of the current message as an off_t, if known.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGetPending
functions.description: Return the number of bytes pending to be read from the internal buffer or socket (exact source unspecified).
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGetReady
functions.description: Return the number of bytes available to read without blocking.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGetRemaining
functions.description: Return the number of bytes remaining to be read for the current message/entity, if known.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGetSecurity
functions.description: Return a string describing the security parameters of the connection, optionally formatting into buffer.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
If buffer is non-NULL, it must point to at least bufsize bytes.
Returned pointer is either buffer or an internal string; do not free internal strings.

functions.name: httpGetState
functions.description: Return the current HTTP protocol state for the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGetStatus
functions.description: Return the last/most recent HTTP status code associated with the connection/response.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGetSubField

name must be a NUL-terminated parameter name.

requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
field must be a valid http_field_t value.
name must be a NUL-terminated parameter name.
value must point to a writable buffer of at least valuelen bytes.
valuelen must be greater than 0 to store any characters.

functions.name: httpGetVersion
functions.description: Return the HTTP protocol version negotiated for the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpGets

functions.name: httpGets2
functions.description: Read a line of text from the connection into line up to length bytes.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
line must point to a writable buffer of at least length bytes.
length must be greater than 0.

functions.name: httpHead
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpWriteRequest). Send an HTTP HEAD request for the given URI.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
uri must be a valid request-target/path or absolute URI.

functions.name: httpIsChunked

functions.name: httpIsEncrypted

requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpOptions

functions.name: httpPost

requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpPut
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpWriteRequest). Send an HTTP PUT request for the given URI.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
uri must be a valid request-target/path or absolute URI.
