functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpRead2). Read up to length bytes from the connection into buffer.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
buffer must point to a writable buffer of at least length bytes.

functions.name: httpRead2

buffer must point to a writable buffer of at least length bytes.
length may be any non-negative size up to the buffer's capacity.

functions.name: httpReconnect

requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpReconnect2

requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
msec is a timeout in milliseconds (exact semantics unknown).

requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

Returned string is owned by the library or is buffer; do not free internal strings.

functions.description: Resolve a URI using CUPS service discovery and options, writing the resolved URI into resolved_uri. Returns resolved_uri or another internal string pointer.
requirements: uri must be a valid input URI string.
resolved_uri must point to a writable buffer of at least resolved_size bytes.
resolved_size must be sufficient to hold the resolved URI including NUL.
options is a bitfield of http_resolve_t values controlling resolution.
cb may be NULL or a callback invoked during resolution; cb_data is passed to it.

functions.name: httpSaveCredentials
functions.signature: int httpSaveCredentials(const char *path, cups_array_t *credentials, const char *common_name);
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use cupsSaveCredentials). Save the provided credentials to disk at path, optionally associated with a common name.
requirements: path must be a valid filesystem path for storage.
credentials must be a valid credentials array.
common_name may be NULL or a NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: httpSeparate
functions.signature: void httpSeparate(const char *uri, char *method, char *username, char *host, int *port, char *resource);
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpSeparateURI). Split a URI into method, username, host, port, and resource components (older interface without explicit lengths).
requirements: uri must be a valid URI string.
Output pointers (method, username, host, port, resource) should be non-NULL if data is desired; buffers must be large enough, but sizes are not specified in this overload.

functions.name: httpSeparate2
functions.signature: void httpSeparate2(const char *uri, char *method, int methodlen, char *username, int usernamelen, char *host, int hostlen, int *port, char *resource, int resourcelen);
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpSeparateURI). Split a URI into components, writing into provided buffers with explicit lengths.
requirements: uri must be a valid URI string.
If method is non-NULL, it must have at least methodlen bytes.
If username is non-NULL, it must have at least usernamelen bytes.
If host is non-NULL, it must have at least hostlen bytes.
If resource is non-NULL, it must have at least resourcelen bytes.
If port is non-NULL, it will receive the parsed port.
Each length parameter must reflect the actual buffer size to avoid overflow.

functions.name: httpSeparateURI
functions.signature: http_uri_status_t httpSeparateURI(http_uri_coding_t decoding, const char *uri, char *scheme, int schemelen, char *username, int usernamelen, char *host, int hostlen, int *port, char *resource, int resourcelen);
functions.description: Split a URI into its components, optionally decoding as specified, writing into provided buffers.
requirements: uri must be a valid URI string.
If scheme is non-NULL, it must have at least schemelen bytes.
If username is non-NULL, it must have at least usernamelen bytes.
If host is non-NULL, it must have at least hostlen bytes.
If resource is non-NULL, it must have at least resourcelen bytes.
If port is non-NULL, it will receive the parsed port.
decoding controls which parts are decoded; choose from http_uri_coding_t.
Each output buffer length must be sufficient; otherwise an appropriate HTTP_URI_STATUS_* error may be returned.

functions.name: httpSetAuthString
functions.signature: void httpSetAuthString(http_t *http, const char *scheme, const char *data);
functions.description: Set the Authorization header string for the connection using the given scheme and data.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
scheme must be a NUL-terminated auth scheme name (e.g., "Basic", "Digest", "Bearer").
data must be a NUL-terminated parameter string appropriate for the scheme.

functions.name: httpSetBlocking
functions.description: Enable or disable blocking I/O on the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpSetCookie
functions.description: Set the Cookie header value for the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
cookie must be a NUL-terminated cookie header value string.

functions.name: httpSetCredentials
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use cupsSetClientCredentials). Set client credentials/certificates on the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
certs must be a valid credentials/certificate array.

functions.name: httpSetDefaultField
functions.signature: void httpSetDefaultField(http_t *http, http_field_t field, const char *value);
functions.description: Set a default HTTP header field value for subsequent requests on this connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
field must be a valid http_field_t value.
value must be a NUL-terminated string or NULL to clear (exact NULL semantics unknown).

functions.name: httpSetEncryption
functions.description: Set or negotiate encryption on the connection according to policy e.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
e must be a valid http_encryption_t value.

functions.name: httpSetExpect
functions.description: Set the expected status (e.g., 100-continue) or internal expectation for the next request.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
expect must be a valid http_status_t value.

functions.name: httpSetField
functions.signature: void httpSetField(http_t *http, http_field_t field, const char *value);
functions.description: Set a specific HTTP header field value for the next request.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
field must be a valid http_field_t value.
value must be a NUL-terminated string or NULL to clear (exact NULL semantics unknown).

functions.name: httpSetKeepAlive
functions.description: Enable or disable HTTP keep-alive on the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
keep_alive must be a valid http_keepalive_t value.

functions.name: httpSetLength
functions.description: Set the Content-Length for the request/response body to be sent/read.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
length must reflect the exact number of bytes expected to send/read when using length-based transfers.

functions.name: httpSetTimeout
functions.signature: void httpSetTimeout(http_t *http, double timeout, http_timeout_cb_t cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Set the I/O timeout (in seconds) and an optional timeout callback for the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
timeout is a non-negative number of seconds (exact semantics for 0 unspecified).
cb may be NULL or a valid callback; user_data is passed to cb.

functions.name: httpShutdown
functions.description: Shut down the connection (e.g., half-close) without freeing the http_t object.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpStateString
functions.description: Return a human-readable string for an HTTP protocol state value.
requirements: state must be a valid http_state_t value.
Returned pointer is a static string; do not modify or free.

functions.name: httpStatus
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpStatusString). Return a human-readable string for an HTTP status code.
requirements: status must be a valid http_status_t value.
Returned pointer is a static string; do not modify or free.

functions.name: httpStatusString
functions.description: Return a human-readable string for an HTTP status code.
requirements: status must be a valid http_status_t value.
Returned pointer is a static string; do not modify or free.

functions.name: httpTrace
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpWriteRequest). Send an HTTP TRACE request for the given URI.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
uri must be a valid request-target/path or absolute URI.

functions.name: httpUpdate
functions.description: Update the connection state, reading/writing as needed and returning the current status.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.

functions.name: httpURIStatusString
functions.description: Return a human-readable string for a URI parsing/assembly status value.
requirements: status must be a valid http_uri_status_t value.
Returned pointer is a static string; do not modify or free.

functions.name: httpWait
functions.description: Wait for I/O readiness on the connection up to msec milliseconds.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
msec is a timeout in milliseconds; non-negative value expected (exact semantics for -1/0 unknown).

functions.name: httpWrite
functions.signature: int httpWrite(http_t *http, const char *buffer, int length);
functions.description: DEPRECATED (use httpWrite2). Write up to length bytes from buffer to the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
buffer must point to at least length bytes of data.
length must be greater than 0 to write any data.

functions.name: httpWrite2
functions.signature: ssize_t httpWrite2(http_t *http, const char *buffer, size_t length);
functions.description: Write up to length bytes from buffer to the connection. Returns number of bytes written or a negative value on error.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
buffer must point to at least length bytes of data to write.
length may be any non-negative size.

functions.name: httpWriteRequest
functions.signature: bool httpWriteRequest(http_t *http, const char *method, const char *uri);
functions.description: Send an HTTP request line and headers for the given method and URI on the connection. Use httpSetField/httpSetLength/etc. prior to call as needed.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection.
method must be a valid HTTP method token (e.g., "GET", "POST", ...).
uri must be a valid request-target/path or absolute URI per server expectations.
Caller should follow with writing the message body (if any) using httpWrite2 and finalize per protocol.

functions.name: httpWriteResponse
functions.description: Write an HTTP response status line and headers for the specified status on a server-side connection.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t connection in a server context.
status must be a valid http_status_t value representing the response code.
Headers should be set beforehand using httpSetField/httpSetLength as appropriate.

functions.name: cupsRasterClose
functions.description: Closes a CUPS raster stream previously opened with cupsRasterOpen or cupsRasterOpenIO and releases associated resources. After closing, the raster handle must not be used. Typically called once all headers and pixel data have been processed.
requirements: r must be a valid raster handle returned by cupsRasterOpen or cupsRasterOpenIO.
Do not use r after this call completes.
If the stream was opened for writing, ensure all intended headers and pixels have been written before closing (inferred).

functions.name: cupsRasterErrorString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string for the last CUPS raster error. Deprecated: Use cupsRasterGetErrorString instead. Intended for diagnostics after a raster operation fails.
requirements: Call only for diagnostic purposes; function is deprecated in favor of cupsRasterGetErrorString.
The returned pointer refers to internal storage and should not be modified or freed (inferred).

functions.name: cupsRasterGetErrorString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing the most recent CUPS raster error. Use after a raster API call indicates failure to obtain details for logging or user messages.
requirements: The returned pointer refers to internal storage and must not be modified or freed (inferred).
Meaningful only after a prior raster operation has failed (inferred).

functions.name: cupsRasterInitHeader
functions.signature: bool cupsRasterInitHeader(cups_page_header2_t *h, cups_media_t *media, const char *optimize, ipp_quality_t quality, const char *intent, ipp_orient_t orientation, const char *sides, const char *type, int xdpi, int ydpi, const char *sheet_back);
functions.description: Initializes a version 2 CUPS raster page header (cups_page_header2_t) from media and job attributes such as optimization, print quality, rendering intent, orientation, sides, content type, resolution, and back-side handling. Use this to populate a header before writing it with cupsRasterWriteHeader2 or to compute image parameters.
requirements: h must be a non-NULL pointer to a cups_page_header2_t to be filled.
media should reference a valid cups_media_t describing the target media (inferred from parameter type).
xdpi and ydpi should be positive integers specifying device resolution (inferred).
Callers should check the boolean return value and handle failure before using h (inferred).

functions.name: cupsRasterInitPWGHeader
functions.signature: int cupsRasterInitPWGHeader(cups_page_header2_t *h, pwg_media_t *media, const char *type, int xdpi, int ydpi, const char *sides, const char *sheet_back);
functions.description: Initializes a version 2 CUPS raster page header for PWG Raster from PWG media and related attributes. Deprecated: Use cupsRasterInitHeader instead. Typically used before cupsRasterWriteHeader2 when producing PWG Raster output.
requirements: h must be a non-NULL pointer to a cups_page_header2_t to be filled.
media should point to a valid pwg_media_t (inferred).
xdpi and ydpi should be positive integers (inferred).
Check the integer return value to detect initialization failure (non-zero/zero semantics are not documented here; handle generically) (inferred).

functions.name: cupsRasterOpen
functions.description: Opens a CUPS raster stream on an existing file descriptor for reading or writing according to the specified mode (read, write, compressed write, PWG Raster write, Apple Raster write). Returns an opaque raster handle used by other raster API calls.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor with appropriate access (readable for CUPS_RASTER_READ, writable for write modes) (inferred).
mode must be one of CUPS_RASTER_READ, CUPS_RASTER_WRITE, CUPS_RASTER_WRITE_COMPRESSED, CUPS_RASTER_WRITE_PWG, or CUPS_RASTER_WRITE_APPLE.
On failure, the function returns NULL; callers must check for NULL before use (inferred).
The lifetime of fd must cover the usage of the returned cups_raster_t; do not close fd independently while the raster is open (inferred).

functions.name: cupsRasterOpenIO
functions.description: Opens a CUPS raster stream using a caller-provided I/O callback instead of a file descriptor. The callback is invoked to read or write raw bytes depending on mode. Returns an opaque raster handle for subsequent operations.
requirements: iocb must be a non-NULL function matching ssize_t (*)(void *ctx, unsigned char *buffer, size_t length).
The callback must implement the correct semantics for the selected mode: supply bytes into buffer for read mode; consume bytes from buffer for write modes (inferred).
ctx is an opaque pointer passed through to the callback and may be NULL.
mode must be one of the defined cups_raster_mode_t values.
On failure, returns NULL; callers must check for NULL (inferred).

functions.name: cupsRasterReadHeader
functions.description: Reads the next page header from a raster stream into a version 1 header structure. Deprecated: Use cupsRasterReadHeader2 with cups_page_header2_t. Typically called once per page before reading pixel data.
requirements: r must be a valid raster handle opened with CUPS_RASTER_READ.
h must be a non-NULL pointer to a cups_page_header_t to receive data.
Callers should check the return value; a value of 0 typically indicates end-of-file or failure (inferred).

functions.name: cupsRasterReadHeader2
functions.description: Reads the next page header from a raster stream into a version 2 header structure. Use this to obtain per-page parameters before reading pixels.
requirements: r must be a valid raster handle opened with CUPS_RASTER_READ.
h must be a non-NULL pointer to a cups_page_header2_t to receive data.
Callers should check the return value; a value of 0 typically indicates end-of-file or failure (inferred).

functions.name: cupsRasterReadPixels
functions.signature: unsigned cupsRasterReadPixels(cups_raster_t *r, unsigned char *p, unsigned len);
functions.description: Reads up to len bytes of raster pixel data from the current page into the buffer p. Typically used after a successful cupsRasterReadHeader/2, reading line-by-line or banded according to the header's bytes-per-line and height.
requirements: r must be a valid raster handle opened with CUPS_RASTER_READ.
p must be a non-NULL buffer with capacity of at least len bytes.
len must be greater than 0 (inferred).
Callers should use header fields (e.g., cupsBytesPerLine, cupsHeight) to determine how many bytes to read per row/band (inferred).
Check the return value; fewer than len bytes or 0 may indicate end-of-page/stream or an error (inferred).

functions.name: cupsRasterWriteHeader
functions.description: Writes a version 1 page header to the raster stream. Deprecated: Use cupsRasterWriteHeader2 with cups_page_header2_t. Call before writing pixel data for a page.
requirements: r must be a valid raster handle opened in a write mode (CUPS_RASTER_WRITE, CUPS_RASTER_WRITE_COMPRESSED, CUPS_RASTER_WRITE_PWG, or CUPS_RASTER_WRITE_APPLE as appropriate).
h must be a non-NULL pointer to a properly initialized cups_page_header_t.
Callers should check the return value for success (non-zero) vs failure (0) (inferred).

functions.name: cupsRasterWriteHeader2
functions.description: Writes a version 2 page header to the raster stream. Call before writing pixel data for each page. Supports PWG and Apple Raster write modes when selected at open time.
requirements: r must be a valid raster handle opened in an appropriate write mode.
h must be a non-NULL pointer to a properly initialized cups_page_header2_t.
Callers should check the return value for success (non-zero) vs failure (0) (inferred).

functions.name: cupsRasterWritePixels
functions.signature: unsigned cupsRasterWritePixels(cups_raster_t *r, unsigned char *p, unsigned len);
functions.description: Writes len bytes of raster pixel data from buffer p to the current page on the raster stream. Typically used after cupsRasterWriteHeader/2, writing line-by-line or in bands as defined by the header.
requirements: r must be a valid raster handle opened in a write mode.
p must be a non-NULL buffer with at least len bytes of pixel data.
len must be greater than 0 (inferred).
Callers should organize writes according to header fields (e.g., cupsBytesPerLine, cupsRowCount/Feed/Step) (inferred).
Check the return value; fewer than len bytes or 0 indicates failure (inferred).

functions.name: cupsThreadGetData
functions.description: Returns the calling thread’s thread-specific data pointer associated with the given key. Implemented as a macro that maps to pthread_getspecific (POSIX) or TlsGetValue (Windows).
requirements: k must be a valid thread-specific data key created/initialized by the threading subsystem (exact creation API not shown in this header).
May return NULL either because no value has been set for the calling thread or due to underlying API semantics; callers must handle NULL.
This is a macro; on POSIX the effective return type is void*, on Windows it maps to LPVOID (compatible with void*).

functions.name: cupsThreadSetData
functions.description: Associates a thread-specific data pointer p with the key k for the calling thread. Implemented as a macro that maps to pthread_setspecific (POSIX) or TlsSetValue (Windows).
requirements: k must be a valid thread-specific data key created/initialized by the threading subsystem (exact creation API not shown in this header).
p may be NULL to clear the value for the calling thread.

Return value semantics are platform-dependent because this is a macro: POSIX returns int (0 on success, error number on failure); Windows returns BOOL (nonzero on success, zero on failure). Callers must handle platform-specific success/failure conventions.
This is a macro; effective signature and return type are platform-dependent. The declared signature here reflects POSIX behavior; on Windows, treat the return value as boolean success/failure.

functions.name: cupsCondBroadcast
functions.description: Wakes all threads waiting on the given condition variable.
requirements: cond must be non-NULL and previously initialized with cupsCondInit.
cond must not have been destroyed prior to calling this function.

functions.name: cupsCondDestroy
functions.description: Destroys a condition variable and releases any associated system resources.
requirements: cond must be non-NULL and previously initialized with cupsCondInit.
No threads may be waiting on cond when this function is called.
cond must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: cupsCondInit
functions.description: Initializes a condition variable for use with associated mutexes.
requirements: cond must be non-NULL and point to valid, writable storage.
cond must not already be initialized.
The initialized condition variable must later be destroyed with cupsCondDestroy to release resources.

functions.name: cupsCondWait
functions.description: Waits on the condition variable cond, atomically releasing mutex while waiting and re-acquiring it before returning. Waits up to timeout seconds (relative).
requirements: cond and mutex must be non-NULL and previously initialized with their respective Init functions.
The calling thread must hold mutex before calling this function.
mutex will be released while waiting and re-acquired before this function returns.
timeout is specified in seconds; exact behavior for negative or special values is unknown from this header and must be treated as implementation-defined.
Spurious wakeups may occur; callers should recheck their predicate after return.

functions.name: cupsMutexDestroy
functions.description: Destroys a mutex, releasing any associated system resources.
requirements: mutex must be non-NULL and previously initialized with cupsMutexInit.
The mutex must not be locked by any thread when destroyed.
mutex must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: cupsMutexInit
functions.description: Initializes a mutex for mutual exclusion.
requirements: mutex must be non-NULL and point to valid, writable storage.
mutex must not already be initialized.
The initialized mutex must later be destroyed with cupsMutexDestroy to release resources.

functions.name: cupsMutexLock
functions.description: Acquires the mutex, blocking the calling thread until the lock is obtained.
requirements: mutex must be non-NULL and previously initialized with cupsMutexInit.
The calling thread should not already hold the mutex to avoid deadlock (recursive locking support is unknown from this header).

functions.name: cupsMutexUnlock
functions.description: Releases the mutex previously acquired by the calling thread.
requirements: mutex must be non-NULL and previously initialized with cupsMutexInit.
The calling thread must currently hold the mutex.

functions.name: cupsRWDestroy
functions.description: Destroys a reader/writer lock and releases its resources.
requirements: rwlock must be non-NULL and previously initialized with cupsRWInit.
The lock must not be held by any thread (neither read nor write) when destroyed.
rwlock must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: cupsRWInit
functions.description: Initializes a reader/writer lock for shared (read) and exclusive (write) access control.
requirements: rwlock must be non-NULL and point to valid, writable storage.
rwlock must not already be initialized.
The initialized lock must later be destroyed with cupsRWDestroy to release resources.

functions.name: cupsRWLockRead
functions.description: Acquires the lock for shared (reader) access, allowing concurrent readers but excluding writers.
requirements: rwlock must be non-NULL and previously initialized with cupsRWInit.

functions.name: cupsRWLockWrite
functions.description: Acquires the lock for exclusive (writer) access, excluding all other readers and writers.
requirements: rwlock must be non-NULL and previously initialized with cupsRWInit.

functions.name: cupsRWUnlock
functions.description: Releases a previously acquired reader or writer lock.
requirements: rwlock must be non-NULL and previously initialized with cupsRWInit.
The calling thread must currently hold the lock in either read or write mode.

functions.name: cupsThreadCancel
functions.description: Requests cancellation/termination of the specified thread.
requirements: thread must be a valid thread handle returned by cupsThreadCreate (not CUPS_THREAD_INVALID).
Behavior and timing of cancellation are implementation-defined and may be asynchronous; callers must not assume immediate termination.
Do not cancel a thread that holds critical resources without appropriate cleanup mechanisms.

functions.name: cupsThreadCreate
functions.description: Creates a new thread that starts executing func(arg). Returns a thread handle for subsequent wait or detach.
requirements: func must be non-NULL and match the signature void *(*)(void *).
The returned thread handle must be either joined with cupsThreadWait or detached with cupsThreadDetach to avoid resource leaks.
Any data referenced by arg must remain valid until the new thread has safely copied or no longer needs it.

functions.name: cupsThreadDetach
functions.description: Detaches the given thread so that its resources are automatically released upon exit and it cannot be joined.
requirements: thread must be a valid thread handle returned by cupsThreadCreate.
thread must not have been previously detached or already joined.
After detaching, cupsThreadWait must not be called on the same thread.

functions.name: cupsThreadWait
functions.description: Joins with the specified thread, blocking until it terminates, and returns the thread’s exit value.
requirements: thread must be a valid joinable thread handle returned by cupsThreadCreate.
thread must not have been detached prior to calling this function.
The calling thread must not attempt to join itself.
The returned pointer value is the thread function’s return value; callers must interpret/manage its lifetime appropriately.

functions.name: cupsCharsetToUTF8
functions.signature: extern int	cupsCharsetToUTF8(cups_utf8_t *dest, const char *src, const int maxout, const cups_encoding_t encoding) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Convert a NUL-terminated string in the specified legacy or non-UTF encoding (encoding) to UTF-8, writing the result into dest. Typical usage: supply a source string encoded as indicated by encoding and a destination buffer with capacity limited by maxout. Returns an int (exact success/error semantics not documented here).
requirements: dest must be a valid, writable pointer to a buffer capable of holding up to maxout UTF-8 units (bytes); whether an additional byte is needed for a NUL terminator is unknown from this header.
src must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string encoded according to the cups_encoding_t value provided.
maxout must be a positive integer specifying the maximum number of output units that may be written to dest.
encoding must be a valid cups_encoding_t value; include language.h to obtain the enum definition.
Input data must be valid in the specified source encoding; behavior on invalid sequences is unspecified here.
Caller should check the returned int for success/failure; precise return-value semantics are unknown from this header.

functions.name: cupsUTF8ToCharset
functions.signature: extern int	cupsUTF8ToCharset(char *dest, const cups_utf8_t *src, const int maxout, const cups_encoding_t encoding) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Convert a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string (src) to the specified legacy or non-UTF encoding (encoding), writing the result into dest. Intended for producing text in a target code page/charset. Returns an int (exact success/error semantics not documented here).
requirements: dest must be a valid, writable pointer to a buffer capable of holding up to maxout output units in the target encoding; whether an extra byte/element is reserved for a NUL terminator is unknown from this header.
src must be a valid, NUL-terminated UTF-8 string (sequence of cups_utf8_t).
maxout must be a positive integer specifying the maximum number of output units that may be written to dest.
encoding must be a valid cups_encoding_t value; include language.h to obtain the enum definition.
Input UTF-8 must be well-formed; behavior on invalid UTF-8 is unspecified here.
Caller should check the returned int for success/failure; precise return-value semantics are unknown from this header.

functions.name: cupsUTF8ToUTF32
functions.signature: extern int	cupsUTF8ToUTF32(cups_utf32_t *dest, const cups_utf8_t *src, const int maxout) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Convert a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string (src) to UTF-32, writing UTF-32 code units into dest. Useful for processing text as fixed-width code points. Returns an int (exact success/error semantics not documented here).
requirements: dest must be a valid, writable pointer to a buffer capable of holding up to maxout UTF-32 code units; whether space for a terminating 0 code unit is required is unknown from this header.
src must be a valid, NUL-terminated UTF-8 string (sequence of cups_utf8_t).
maxout must be a positive integer specifying the maximum number of UTF-32 code units that may be written to dest.
Input UTF-8 must be well-formed; behavior on invalid UTF-8 is unspecified here.
Caller should check the returned int for success/failure; precise return-value semantics are unknown from this header.

functions.name: cupsUTF32ToUTF8
functions.signature: extern int	cupsUTF32ToUTF8(cups_utf8_t *dest, const cups_utf32_t *src, const int maxout) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Convert a NUL-terminated UTF-32 string (src) to UTF-8, writing the result into dest. Typical usage: provide a UTF-32 code-unit array terminated by a 0 code unit and a destination buffer limited by maxout. Returns an int (exact success/error semantics not documented here).
requirements: dest must be a valid, writable pointer to a buffer capable of holding up to maxout UTF-8 units (bytes); whether an additional byte is needed for a NUL terminator is unknown from this header.
src must be a valid, NUL-terminated UTF-32 string where termination is a 0 code unit (cups_utf32_t).
maxout must be a positive integer specifying the maximum number of UTF-8 units that may be written to dest.
Input UTF-32 sequence must contain valid Unicode scalar values; behavior on invalid values is unspecified here.
Caller should check the returned int for success/failure; precise return-value semantics are unknown from this header.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDCopyComputerName
functions.description: Copies the local computer name (as used for DNS-SD) into the provided buffer using the given DNS-SD context. Intended for callers that need a stable, user-friendly computer name for service registration or display.
requirements: dnssd must be a valid, initialized cups_dnssd_t context created by cupsDNSSDNew.
buffer must be non-NULL and point to writable storage.
bufsize must be greater than 0 and reflect the size of buffer in bytes.
On failure behavior and return value are not documented here; callers should check the return pointer for NULL to detect errors (inferred from common C patterns).
Thread-safety and lifetime of the returned data (in buffer) depend solely on the caller-managed buffer.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDCopyHostName
functions.description: Copies the local host name (as used for DNS) into the provided buffer using the given DNS-SD context. Useful for constructing SRV/A/AAAA records or logging.
requirements: dnssd must be a valid, initialized cups_dnssd_t context created by cupsDNSSDNew.
buffer must be non-NULL and point to writable storage.
bufsize must be greater than 0 and reflect the size of buffer in bytes.
Return-on-error semantics are not specified; callers should check for a NULL return (inferred from common patterns).

functions.name: cupsDNSSDDelete
functions.description: Destroys a DNS-SD context and releases associated resources.
requirements: dnssd must either be NULL (a no-op in many C APIs; allowance is unknown here) or a valid cups_dnssd_t previously returned by cupsDNSSDNew.
Do not use dnssd or any objects created from it after this call; they become invalid.

All outstanding browse/query/resolve/service objects tied to this context should be deleted or otherwise finalized before deleting the context (not stated, but typical to avoid use-after-free; exact requirement unknown).

functions.name: cupsDNSSDGetConfigChanges
functions.description: Returns a count of configuration changes observed by the DNS-SD context. Typically used to detect network/host changes and refresh state.
requirements: dnssd must be a valid cups_dnssd_t context.
The meaning of the returned size_t (absolute count vs. number since last call) is not documented here and is unknown.
Callers should handle potential wrap-around if used as a monotonically increasing counter (behavior unknown).

functions.name: cupsDNSSDNew
functions.description: Creates a new DNS-SD context for browsing, resolving, querying, and service registration. The optional error callback, if supported, is invoked to report asynchronous errors.
requirements: error_cb function pointer requirements (NULL allowed or not) are not specified here and are unknown.
cb_data is an opaque pointer passed to error_cb; it is not used by the API otherwise.
The returned pointer must be deleted with cupsDNSSDDelete when no longer needed.
The caller must ensure any global initialization required by CUPS (if any) is performed before use (unknown).

functions.name: cupsDNSSDBrowseDelete
functions.description: Cancels and destroys a DNS-SD browse request created with cupsDNSSDBrowseNew.
requirements: browser must be a valid cups_dnssd_browse_t returned by cupsDNSSDBrowseNew.
After return, browser must not be used again.
Any callbacks in flight may race with deletion; concurrency guarantees are not documented and are unknown.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDBrowseGetContext
functions.description: Returns the DNS-SD context associated with a browse request.
requirements: browser must be a valid cups_dnssd_browse_t.
The returned context remains owned by the component that created it; do not delete it via this pointer unless you own it.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDBrowseNew
functions.signature: cups_dnssd_browse_t *cupsDNSSDBrowseNew(cups_dnssd_t *dnssd, uint32_t if_index, const char *types, const char *domain, cups_dnssd_browse_cb_t browse_cb, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Starts a DNS-SD browse for one or more service types in the specified domain and network interface. Results are delivered asynchronously via browse_cb.
requirements: dnssd must be a valid cups_dnssd_t context.
if_index selects the interface; use CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_ANY for all or CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_LOCAL for local-only.
types must point to a valid service type string (format not specified here; likely a regtype such as "_ipp._tcp").
domain must be a valid domain string (e.g., "local."); if NULL is permitted is unknown.
browse_cb is the callback invoked for results; whether it may be NULL is unknown.
cb_data is passed through to browse_cb unchanged by the API.
The returned browse handle must be deleted with cupsDNSSDBrowseDelete.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDQueryDelete
functions.description: Cancels and destroys a DNS query request created with cupsDNSSDQueryNew.
requirements: query must be a valid cups_dnssd_query_t.
After return, query must not be used again.
Callback concurrency and in-flight completion semantics are not documented and are unknown.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDQueryGetContext
functions.description: Returns the DNS-SD context associated with a query request.
requirements: query must be a valid cups_dnssd_query_t.
The context remains owned by its creator; do not delete it via this pointer unless you own it.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDQueryNew
functions.signature: cups_dnssd_query_t *cupsDNSSDQueryNew(cups_dnssd_t *dnssd, uint32_t if_index, const char *fullname, uint16_t rrtype, cups_dnssd_query_cb_t query_cb, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Starts a DNS query for a specific record type of a fully-qualified domain name on the specified interface. Results are delivered asynchronously via query_cb.
requirements: dnssd must be a valid cups_dnssd_t context.
if_index selects the interface; use CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_ANY or CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_LOCAL as needed.
fullname must be a valid FQDN for the query (e.g., a service instance name for TXT/SRV, or a host for A/AAAA).
rrtype must be a valid DNS record type (see cups_dnssd_rrtype_t values).
query_cb is the result callback; whether NULL is allowed is unknown.
cb_data is passed to query_cb.
The returned query handle must be deleted with cupsDNSSDQueryDelete.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDResolveDelete
functions.description: Cancels and destroys a DNS-SD resolve request created with cupsDNSSDResolveNew.
requirements: res must be a valid cups_dnssd_resolve_t.
After return, res must not be used again.
Callback concurrency guarantees are not documented and are unknown.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDResolveGetContext
functions.description: Returns the DNS-SD context associated with a resolve request.
requirements: res must be a valid cups_dnssd_resolve_t.
The context remains owned by its creator; do not delete it via this pointer unless you own it.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDResolveNew
functions.signature: cups_dnssd_resolve_t *cupsDNSSDResolveNew(cups_dnssd_t *dnssd, uint32_t if_index, const char *name, const char *type, const char *domain, cups_dnssd_resolve_cb_t resolve_cb, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Starts resolving a DNS-SD service instance (name/type/domain) to obtain target host, port, and TXT key/value pairs. Results are delivered asynchronously via resolve_cb.
requirements: dnssd must be a valid cups_dnssd_t context.
if_index selects the interface; use CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_ANY or CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_LOCAL as needed.
name must be the service instance name (not FQDN).
type must be the regtype string (e.g., "_ipp._tcp").
domain must be the domain (e.g., "local.").
resolve_cb is the callback for results; whether NULL is allowed is unknown.
cb_data is passed to resolve_cb.
The returned resolve handle must be deleted with cupsDNSSDResolveDelete.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDServiceAdd
functions.signature: bool cupsDNSSDServiceAdd(cups_dnssd_service_t *service, const char *types, const char *domain, const char *host, uint16_t port, int num_txt, cups_option_t *txt);
functions.description: Adds a service entry (or entries) to a service registration object, specifying service type(s), domain, target host, port, and TXT key/value options.
requirements: service must be a valid cups_dnssd_service_t created by cupsDNSSDServiceNew.
types must specify at least one service regtype string (format not documented here; unknown if multiple types are allowed).
domain must be a valid domain string for publication (e.g., "local.").
host must be a valid host name for the SRV target.
port is a TCP/UDP port number; byte order expectations are not stated and are unknown (commonly host byte order).
If num_txt > 0, txt must point to an array of at least num_txt cups_option_t entries.
If num_txt == 0, txt may be NULL or ignored (allowance unknown).
Return value true indicates success, false indicates failure; specific error reporting is via the context’s error callback if provided (inferred).

functions.name: cupsDNSSDServiceDelete
functions.description: Destroys a service registration object and releases associated resources. If published, it will be unpublished.
requirements: service must be a valid cups_dnssd_service_t returned by cupsDNSSDServiceNew.
After return, service must not be used again.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDServiceGetContext
functions.description: Returns the DNS-SD context associated with a service registration object.
requirements: service must be a valid cups_dnssd_service_t.
The returned context remains owned by its creator; do not delete it via this pointer unless you own it.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDServiceGetName
functions.description: Returns the service instance name associated with the service registration object.
requirements: service must be a valid cups_dnssd_service_t.
The returned string’s ownership/lifetime are not documented; treat it as read-only and valid at least until the service object is deleted (inference; exact duration unknown).

functions.name: cupsDNSSDServiceNew
functions.signature: cups_dnssd_service_t *cupsDNSSDServiceNew(cups_dnssd_t *dnssd, uint32_t if_index, const char *name, cups_dnssd_service_cb_t cb, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Creates a new service registration object bound to a DNS-SD context and interface, for later configuration via cupsDNSSDServiceAdd and publication via cupsDNSSDServicePublish. Optional callbacks notify about registration events.
requirements: dnssd must be a valid cups_dnssd_t context.
if_index selects the interface; use CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_ANY or CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_LOCAL as needed.
name must be the service instance name to register.
cb is the service registration callback; whether NULL is allowed is unknown.
cb_data is passed to cb.
The returned service object must be deleted with cupsDNSSDServiceDelete.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDServicePublish
functions.description: Publishes all service entries added to the service registration object to DNS-SD. Typically called after configuring types, domain, host/port, and TXT records.
requirements: service must be a valid cups_dnssd_service_t created by cupsDNSSDServiceNew.
At least one service entry should have been added via cupsDNSSDServiceAdd before publishing (strongly implied; exact requirement unknown).
Returns true on success, false on failure; detailed error reporting may be via the context’s error callback (inferred).

functions.name: cupsDNSSDServiceSetLocation
functions.description: Sets a location/geo URI for the service registration, typically encoded into DNS-SD TXT data or related metadata.
requirements: service must be a valid cups_dnssd_service_t.
geo_uri must be a valid, NUL-terminated string representing a location (format not specified; commonly a geo: URI).
Returns true on success, false on failure; specific error causes are not documented here.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDAssembleFullName
functions.signature: bool cupsDNSSDAssembleFullName(char *fullname, size_t fullsize, const char *name, const char *type, const char *domain);
functions.description: Constructs a fully-qualified service instance name from separate name, type (regtype), and domain components and writes it into fullname.
requirements: fullname must be non-NULL and point to a writable buffer.
fullsize must be greater than 0 and reflect the size of fullname in bytes.
name, type, and domain must be valid, NUL-terminated strings; formatting/escaping rules for DNS-SD labels are not specified here and are unknown.
Returns true on success and false on error (e.g., buffer too small) by common convention; exact failure conditions are not documented here.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDDecodeTXT
functions.signature: int cupsDNSSDDecodeTXT(const unsigned char *txtrec, uint16_t txtlen, cups_option_t **txt);
functions.description: Parses a raw DNS-SD TXT record into an array of cups_option_t key/value pairs, returning the number of pairs parsed.
requirements: txtrec must point to txtlen bytes containing a valid DNS-SD TXT record in wire format (length-prefixed strings).
txtlen is the number of bytes available at txtrec.
txt must be a non-NULL pointer to receive an allocated array of cups_option_t entries; the allocation and freeing rules are not documented here and are unknown (commonly freed with cupsFreeOptions).
Returns the number of options on success; negative values or zero-on-error semantics are not specified here and are unknown.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDSeparateFullName
functions.signature: bool cupsDNSSDSeparateFullName(const char *fullname, char *name, size_t namesize, char *type, size_t typesize, char *domain, size_t domainsize);
functions.description: Splits a fully-qualified service instance name into name, type (regtype), and domain components, writing each into the provided buffers.
requirements: fullname must be a valid, NUL-terminated string containing a full service name.
name, type, and domain must point to writable buffers; any of them may be NULL to skip output (allowance unknown).
namesize, typesize, and domainsize must reflect the sizes of their respective buffers; must be > 0 for any non-NULL buffer.
Returns true on success and false on error (e.g., buffers too small or malformed fullname) by common convention; exact failure conditions are not documented here.

functions.name: cupsFormDecode
functions.description: Decodes URL-encoded form data into a CUPS option list. Intended to parse a form/query string (e.g., application/x-www-form-urlencoded) and populate an array of cups_option_t pairs that represent the form variables. Typical usage: pass a null-terminated form data string and receive an allocated options array via vars, with the return value indicating how many options were decoded (exact error/return semantics are not documented here).
requirements: data must be a valid, null-terminated C string containing form data encoded in a URL-compatible format (likely application/x-www-form-urlencoded).
vars must be a non-NULL pointer to a cups_option_t* variable that can be written to by the function.

The function will allocate or set *vars to reference option storage; the caller should assume ownership and free it using cupsFreeOptions(return_value, *vars) if the return value is a non-negative count, consistent with common CUPS option APIs.
If no variables are present, callers should be prepared for a return value of 0 and *vars possibly set to NULL or a valid empty list (exact behavior is not specified).

Error handling and return conventions are not documented in the provided header; callers should check the returned int for non-negative counts and treat negative values as errors (inferred from common CUPS patterns).

functions.name: cupsFormEncode
functions.signature: extern char *cupsFormEncode(const char *url, int num_vars, cups_option_t *vars);
functions.description: Encodes the provided CUPS option list as URL form parameters and combines them with a base URL. Intended to build a URL containing a query string derived from num_vars entries in vars. Returns a newly allocated C string containing the encoded URL, or NULL on failure (exact allocation/ownership details are not documented here but commonly the caller frees the result).
requirements: url should be a valid, null-terminated base URL string; behavior for NULL is unspecified.
num_vars should be >= 0 and represent the number of valid elements in vars (inferred from typical CUPS option list usage).
vars should point to at least num_vars valid cups_option_t entries; if num_vars is 0, vars may be NULL (inferred).
The returned char* is dynamically allocated; the caller should free it using free() when no longer needed (inferred from common CUPS API conventions for returned strings).
Parameters names and values should be representable as URL-encoded strings; characters outside unreserved sets will be percent-encoded (inferred from function purpose).
On failure, callers should handle a NULL return value (exact error conditions are not specified).

functions.name: cupsAddDest
functions.signature: int cupsAddDest(const char *name, const char *instance, int num_dests, cups_dest_t **dests);
functions.description: Adds (or ensures) a destination entry in the array of destinations. Returns updated count. Typical usage is to insert a printer/class (optionally with an instance) into an existing dests list.
requirements: dests must be a valid pointer to a cups_dest_t* variable (address of the array pointer).
num_dests must be >= 0 and correspond to the current number of entries in *dests.
name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
If memory is (re)allocated, caller is responsible for later freeing with cupsFreeDests(num_dests, dests).

functions.name: cupsAddDestMediaOptions
functions.signature: int cupsAddDestMediaOptions(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *dinfo, unsigned flags, cups_size_t *size, int num_options, cups_option_t **options);
functions.description: Deprecated. Adds media-related IPP options for the specified destination using an old cups_size_t media struct. Prefer cupsAddDestMediaOptions2. Returns updated number of options.
requirements: dest must point to a valid destination; dinfo should correspond to dest (from cupsCopyDestInfo).
options must be a valid pointer to a cups_option_t* variable; num_options must be >= 0.
size should point to a valid cups_size_t describing desired media.
flags is a bitwise combination of cups_media_flags_t.
http may be NULL to use default connection or a valid HTTP connection.

functions.name: cupsAddDestMediaOptions2
functions.signature: int cupsAddDestMediaOptions2(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *dinfo, unsigned flags, cups_media_t *media, int num_options, cups_option_t **options);
functions.description: Adds media-related IPP options for a destination using the newer cups_media_t structure. Returns updated number of options in the options array.
requirements: dest must point to a valid destination; dinfo should be obtained for that dest (e.g., cupsCopyDestInfo/2).
media must point to a valid cups_media_t describing desired media.
options must be a valid pointer to a cups_option_t* variable; num_options must be >= 0.
flags is a bitwise combination of cups_media_flags_t.
http may be NULL or a valid HTTP connection.

functions.name: cupsAddIntegerOption
functions.signature: int cupsAddIntegerOption(const char *name, int value, int num_options, cups_option_t **options);
functions.description: Appends an integer-valued option (converted to a string) to an options array. Returns updated count.
requirements: name must be non-NULL.
options must be a valid pointer to a cups_option_t* variable.
num_options must be >= 0.

functions.name: cupsAddOption
functions.signature: int cupsAddOption(const char *name, const char *value, int num_options, cups_option_t **options);
functions.description: Appends a name/value option to an options array. Returns updated count.
requirements: name must be non-NULL; value may be NULL depending on option semantics.
options must be a valid pointer to a cups_option_t* variable.
num_options must be >= 0.

functions.name: cupsAreCredentialsValidForName
functions.description: Checks whether the provided credentials are valid for the given X.509 common name. Returns true if valid.
requirements: common_name must be non-NULL.
credentials must reference credential material in a form accepted by CUPS (exact format unspecified in this header).

functions.name: cupsCancelDestJob
functions.description: Cancels a job identified by job_id on the specified destination using IPP via the given HTTP connection. Returns an IPP status code.
requirements: http must be a valid connection; dest must refer to a valid destination.
job_id must be a job identifier (typically > 0).

functions.name: cupsCancelJob
functions.description: Cancels a job by destination name and job_id using the default connection. Returns 0 on failure or a non-negative result depending on implementation (exact convention not specified here).
requirements: name must be non-NULL and name a printer/class.
job_id must be a job identifier.

functions.name: cupsCancelJob2
functions.signature: ipp_status_t cupsCancelJob2(http_t *http, const char *name, int job_id, int purge);
functions.description: Cancels a job by name and job_id via the supplied HTTP connection, optionally purging it immediately. Returns an IPP status code.
requirements: http must be a valid HTTP connection.
name must be non-NULL.
job_id must be a job identifier.
purge controls purge behavior (non-zero to purge).

functions.name: cupsCheckDestSupported
functions.signature: int cupsCheckDestSupported(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *info, const char *option, const char *value);
functions.description: Checks whether a destination supports a given option/value pair using printer capability info. Returns non-zero/zero (exact semantics not detailed here).
requirements: http may be NULL or valid; dest must be valid; info must correspond to dest (e.g., from cupsCopyDestInfo/2).
option must be non-NULL; value may be NULL if checking option-only support is allowed by implementation.

functions.name: cupsCloseDestJob
functions.signature: ipp_status_t cupsCloseDestJob(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *info, int job_id);
functions.description: Closes/finalizes a job previously created on a destination. Returns an IPP status code.
requirements: http must be a valid connection; dest and info must be valid and consistent.
job_id must be the identifier returned by cupsCreateDestJob.

functions.name: cupsConcatString
functions.signature: size_t cupsConcatString(char *dst, const char *src, size_t dstsize);
functions.description: Appends src to dst with size-limited concatenation, returning the length of the resulting string or total length that would have been created. Safe string helper.
requirements: dst must be a valid, writable buffer with size dstsize bytes.
src and dst must be NUL-terminated strings if present.
dstsize specifies the full size of the dst buffer and should be > 0 to store data.

functions.name: cupsConnectDest
functions.signature: http_t *cupsConnectDest(cups_dest_t *dest, unsigned flags, int msec, int *cancel, char *resource, size_t resourcesize, cups_dest_cb_t cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Connects to the specified destination, optionally returning the resolved resource path, honoring flags/timeouts, and issuing progress via callback. Returns an HTTP connection handle or NULL on error.
requirements: dest must be a valid destination.
flags is a bitwise combination of cups_dest_flags_t.
msec is a timeout in milliseconds; may be 0 for default behavior.
cancel may be NULL or point to an int set non-zero to cancel.

resourcesize must reflect the size of resource in bytes when resource is non-NULL.
cb may be NULL or a valid cups_dest_cb_t; user_data is passed through to the callback.

functions.name: cupsConnectDestBlock
functions.signature: http_t *cupsConnectDestBlock(cups_dest_t *dest, unsigned flags, int msec, int *cancel, char *resource, size_t resourcesize, cups_dest_block_t block);
functions.description: Deprecated (blocks version). Connects to a destination using a blocks-based callback on platforms supporting blocks. Returns an HTTP connection or NULL.
requirements: Only available when compiled with __BLOCKS__.
dest must be valid.
flags is a bitwise combination of cups_dest_flags_t.
msec is a timeout in milliseconds.
cancel may be NULL or valid pointer to a cancel flag.
resource/resourcesize behave like cupsConnectDest.
block may be NULL or a valid blocks callback.

functions.name: cupsCopyCredentials
functions.description: Copies credentials (certificate bundle) for the specified common name from the given path into a newly-allocated file/directory and returns the path string. Caller must free the returned string.
requirements: path must be a valid filesystem path.
common_name must be non-NULL.
Caller must free the returned char* with free().

functions.name: cupsCopyCredentialsKey
functions.description: Copies the private key associated with the credentials for the given common name at path and returns the path to the copied key. Caller frees the returned string.
requirements: path must be a valid path containing credentials.
common_name must be non-NULL.
Caller must free the returned char*.

functions.name: cupsCopyCredentialsPublicKey
functions.description: Copies the public key from the credentials for the given common name at path and returns the path to the copied public key. Caller frees the returned string.
requirements: path must be valid.
common_name must be non-NULL.
Caller must free returned char*.

functions.name: cupsCopyCredentialsRequest
functions.description: Copies a credentials request (CSR) for the given common name from path to a new location and returns the path string. Caller frees the returned string.
requirements: path must be valid.
common_name must be non-NULL.
Caller must free returned char*.

functions.name: cupsCopyDest
functions.description: Adds a copy of the specified destination to the dests array. Returns updated count.
requirements: dest must be a valid destination to copy.
dests must be a valid pointer to a cups_dest_t* variable; num_dests must be >= 0.
Caller later frees with cupsFreeDests.

functions.name: cupsCopyDestConflicts
functions.signature: int cupsCopyDestConflicts(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *info, int num_options, cups_option_t *options, const char *new_option, const char *new_value, int *num_conflicts, cups_option_t **conflicts, int *num_resolved, cups_option_t **resolved);
functions.description: Analyzes option conflicts for a destination when applying a new option/value. Populates conflicts/resolved arrays and returns a status/int value (exact semantics unspecified here).
requirements: http may be NULL or valid.
dest and info must be valid and consistent.
options must be a valid array of length num_options (num_options >= 0).
new_option must be non-NULL; new_value may be NULL depending on option semantics.
num_conflicts and conflicts must be valid pointers if conflict results are requested; same for num_resolved and resolved.
Caller must free any returned conflicts/resolved arrays with cupsFreeOptions.

functions.name: cupsCopyDestInfo
functions.description: Fetches and returns a copy of destination capability/status information for a destination. Caller must free with cupsFreeDestInfo.
requirements: http may be NULL or a valid HTTP connection.
dest must be a valid destination pointer.
Caller must release the returned cups_dinfo_t* with cupsFreeDestInfo.

functions.name: cupsCopyDestInfo2
functions.description: Like cupsCopyDestInfo but allows specifying destination flags for retrieval behavior. Returns destination info object to be freed by caller.
requirements: http may be NULL or valid.
dest must be valid.
dflags is a bitwise combination of cups_dest_flags_t.
Caller must free the result with cupsFreeDestInfo.

functions.name: cupsCopyString
functions.signature: size_t cupsCopyString(char *dst, const char *src, size_t dstsize);
functions.description: Copies src into dst with size limit, always NUL-terminating if dstsize > 0. Returns length of the copied/required string. Safe string copy helper.
requirements: dst must be a writable buffer of size dstsize bytes.
src must be a NUL-terminated string (may be NULL only if implementation allows; not specified here).
dstsize should be > 0 to store data.

functions.name: cupsCreateCredentials
functions.signature: bool cupsCreateCredentials(const char *path, bool ca_cert, cups_credpurpose_t purpose, cups_credtype_t type, cups_credusage_t usage, const char *organization, const char *org_unit, const char *locality, const char *state_province, const char *country, const char *common_name, const char *email, size_t num_alt_names, const char * const *alt_names, const char *root_name, time_t expiration_date);
functions.description: Creates X.509 credentials (certificate and key), optionally a CA certificate, with specified purpose, type, usage, subject attributes, SANs, and expiration. Writes to path. Returns true on success.

purpose/usage/type must be valid enum combinations.

email may be NULL or string; num_alt_names and alt_names specify SANs (num_alt_names is the count of entries in alt_names).
root_name may specify parent CA/common name for signing; semantics not detailed here.
expiration_date is a time_t defining validity end date.

functions.name: cupsCreateCredentialsRequest
functions.signature: bool cupsCreateCredentialsRequest(const char *path, cups_credpurpose_t purpose, cups_credtype_t type, cups_credusage_t usage, const char *organization, const char *org_unit, const char *locality, const char *state_province, const char *country, const char *common_name, const char *email, size_t num_alt_names, const char * const *alt_names);
functions.description: Creates a certificate signing request (CSR) at path with the given subject, SANs, and credential parameters. Returns true on success.
requirements: path must be writable/valid.
purpose/type/usage must be valid enum values.
common_name should be non-NULL; other subject fields as needed.
num_alt_names must match entries of alt_names (may be 0 with alt_names NULL).

functions.name: cupsCreateDestJob
functions.signature: ipp_status_t cupsCreateDestJob(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *info, int *job_id, const char *title, int num_options, cups_option_t *options);
functions.description: Creates a print job on the specified destination and returns the new job ID via job_id. Returns IPP status.

dest and info must be valid and consistent.

title may be NULL or a job title string.
options must point to an array of length num_options (num_options >= 0).

functions.name: cupsCreateJob
functions.signature: int cupsCreateJob(http_t *http, const char *name, const char *title, int num_options, cups_option_t *options);
functions.description: Creates a print job on the named destination via the given HTTP connection. Returns the job ID or a negative/zero value on error (exact semantics not stated here).
requirements: http must be a valid HTTP connection.
name must be non-NULL destination name.
title may be NULL.
options must point to an array of length num_options; num_options >= 0.

functions.name: cupsCreateTempFd
functions.signature: int cupsCreateTempFd(const char *prefix, const char *suffix, char *filename, size_t len);
functions.description: Creates a secure temporary file and returns an open file descriptor. If filename buffer is provided, writes the path. Returns -1 on error.
requirements: prefix/suffix may be NULL or strings influencing the temp name; not strictly required by this header.
filename may be NULL or a writable buffer of size len bytes to receive the path; len must reflect the buffer size.

requirements: ppd must be a valid opened ppd_file_t.
name must be a non-NULL page size name string.

functions.name: ppdSetConformance
functions.description: Sets the PPD parser conformance mode (relaxed or strict) affecting subsequent parsing behavior. Deprecated.
requirements: c must be a valid ppd_conform_t value (PPD_CONFORM_RELAXED or PPD_CONFORM_STRICT).
Call before parsing if strictness must be enforced for ppdOpen* calls.

functions.name: cupsBackChannelRead
functions.signature: extern ssize_t cupsBackChannelRead(char *buffer, size_t bytes, double timeout);
functions.description: Reads printer/device back-channel data into buffer. Intended for use in CUPS backends/filters to receive asynchronous status or device responses. Returns the number of bytes read (ssize_t), or a negative value on error (inferred POSIX convention). Timeout is in seconds.
requirements: buffer must be a valid, writable pointer to at least bytes bytes.
bytes must reflect the maximum number of bytes that can be written to buffer; bytes may be 0 if no data is desired.
timeout is a duration in seconds; the exact behavior for 0 or negative values is not documented here (unknown).
Should be called in an environment where a CUPS back-channel is available (e.g., from a CUPS backend/filter). Behavior when no back-channel is present is not specified (unknown).
Caller must handle partial reads and retry if necessary (common for non-blocking/timeout I/O; inferred).

functions.name: cupsBackChannelWrite
functions.signature: extern ssize_t cupsBackChannelWrite(const char *buffer, size_t bytes, double timeout);
functions.description: Writes data to the CUPS back-channel (typically from a backend to filters or upstream components). Returns the number of bytes written (ssize_t), or a negative value on error (inferred POSIX convention). Timeout is in seconds.
requirements: buffer must be a valid pointer to at least bytes bytes of readable memory; may be NULL only if bytes is 0.
bytes is the number of bytes to write; must not exceed the readable region of buffer.
timeout is a duration in seconds; exact behavior for 0 or negative values is not documented here (unknown).
Should be used in a CUPS environment where the back-channel is supported by the connection/backend; otherwise writes may fail (unknown specifics).
Caller must handle partial writes and retry if necessary (inferred for timeout/non-blocking semantics).

functions.name: cupsSideChannelDoRequest
functions.signature: extern cups_sc_status_t cupsSideChannelDoRequest(cups_sc_command_t command, char *data, int *datalen, double timeout);
functions.description: Sends a single side-channel command to the backend/device and optionally exchanges data, completing the request and returning a status. Used to perform operations like soft reset, drain output, query bidirectional capability, device ID, state, SNMP, or connected status.
requirements: command must be a valid cups_sc_command_t value (e.g., CUPS_SC_CMD_SOFT_RESET, CUPS_SC_CMD_GET_DEVICE_ID, etc.).
data may be NULL if the command does not send/return data; when non-NULL, it must point to a writable buffer of at least *datalen bytes capacity on input.

datalen must be non-NULL when data is provided; on input, *datalen specifies the size of the data buffer; on success it may be updated with the number of bytes written/returned (behavior inferred from common CUPS patterns; exact details not documented here).
timeout is in seconds; exact semantics for 0 or negative values are not documented here (unknown).
Caller must check the returned cups_sc_status_t to determine success/failure and handle errors accordingly.
For commands that return data (e.g., GET_DEVICE_ID), ensure the buffer is sufficiently large; overflow is prevented by providing accurate *datalen capacity.

functions.name: cupsSideChannelRead
functions.signature: extern int cupsSideChannelRead(cups_sc_command_t *command, cups_sc_status_t *status, char *data, int *datalen, double timeout);
functions.description: Receives a side-channel message, returning the command and status along with optional data. Intended for backends/filters that need to process side-channel traffic. Returns an int; exact return-value conventions are not documented here (unknown).
requirements: command must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the cups_sc_command_t of the incoming message.
status must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the cups_sc_status_t associated with the message.
data may be NULL if the caller does not wish to receive data; if non-NULL it must point to a writable buffer of at least *datalen bytes.

datalen must be non-NULL when data is provided; on input, *datalen specifies the size of the data buffer; on return, it may be updated with the number of bytes received (behavior inferred; exact details not documented here).
timeout is in seconds; behavior for 0 or negative values is not documented here (unknown).
Caller must handle the case where the incoming data exceeds the provided buffer (status/return may indicate truncation or error; exact behavior unknown).

functions.name: cupsSideChannelSNMPGet
functions.signature: extern cups_sc_status_t cupsSideChannelSNMPGet(const char *oid, char *data, int *datalen, double timeout);
functions.description: Performs an SNMP GET for the specified OID via the CUPS side-channel and returns the value bytes in data. Returns a cups_sc_status_t indicating success or error.
requirements: oid must be a valid, NUL-terminated OID string identifying a single SNMP object (commonly a numeric OID such as "1.3.6.1...").
data must point to a writable buffer capable of holding up to *datalen bytes; may be NULL only if *datalen is 0 (useful to query required size if supported; actual support unknown).
datalen must be non-NULL; on input, *datalen specifies the size of the data buffer; on success, it may be updated with the length of the returned value (inferred; exact details not documented here).
timeout is in seconds; exact semantics for 0 or negative are not documented here (unknown).
Caller must check the returned cups_sc_status_t for success (CUPS_SC_STATUS_OK) before using data (status codes are defined in cups_sc_status_t).

functions.name: cupsSideChannelSNMPWalk
functions.signature: extern cups_sc_status_t cupsSideChannelSNMPWalk(const char *oid, double timeout, cups_sc_walk_func_t cb, void *context);
functions.description: Performs an SNMP WALK starting at the given OID, invoking cb for each returned varbind/value. The callback receives the OID string, a pointer to the value bytes, its length, and the user-supplied context. Returns a cups_sc_status_t for overall success/error.
requirements: oid must be a valid, NUL-terminated OID string specifying the subtree root to walk.
cb must be a valid function pointer; it will be called zero or more times with (oid, data, datalen, context).
The callback must not assume data is NUL-terminated; datalen provides the exact length.
context is an opaque pointer passed through to cb and may be NULL.
timeout is in seconds; exact semantics (overall vs per-step) are not documented here (unknown).
The callback must return quickly and be reentrant/thread-safe if used in multi-threaded contexts (general guidance; not specified here).
Caller must check the returned cups_sc_status_t and handle errors/timeouts accordingly.

functions.name: cupsSideChannelWrite
functions.signature: extern int cupsSideChannelWrite(cups_sc_command_t command, cups_sc_status_t status, const char *data, int datalen, double timeout);
functions.description: Sends a side-channel message with the given command, status, and optional data to the peer over the CUPS side-channel. Intended for backends/filters to communicate side-channel information. Returns an int; exact return-value conventions are not documented here (unknown).
requirements: command must be a valid cups_sc_command_t value.
status must be a valid cups_sc_status_t representing the message status.
data may be NULL if datalen is 0; otherwise must point to at least datalen bytes of readable memory.
datalen must be >= 0; when 0, no data is sent.
timeout is in seconds; behavior for 0 or negative values is not documented here (unknown).
Caller should ensure that data length and types are appropriate for the specified command (e.g., device ID queries/returns), as peers may expect specific formats (inferred from command set).

functions.name: cupsAdminCreateWindowsPPD
functions.signature: char *cupsAdminCreateWindowsPPD(http_t *http, const char *dest, char *buffer, int bufsize);
functions.description: Deprecated. Creates or retrieves a Windows PPD for the specified CUPS destination and writes/returns a path string via the provided buffer. Intended for legacy Windows driver workflows. Returns a pointer (typically to the provided buffer) on success, or NULL on failure. Usage: connect to the CUPS server (http), supply the destination name, and provide a writable buffer and its size to receive the resulting PPD filename/path.
requirements: http must be a valid/initialized CUPS HTTP connection (http_t*).
dest should be a valid, existing destination/printer name string.
buffer must be a writable, non-NULL character buffer.
bufsize must be greater than 0 and reflect the actual size of buffer.
Function is deprecated; prefer newer workflows/APIs where available.
Caller should check for a NULL return to detect failure.

functions.name: cupsAdminExportSamba
functions.signature: int cupsAdminExportSamba(const char *dest, const char *ppd, const char *samba_server, const char *samba_user, const char *samba_password, FILE *logfile);
functions.description: Deprecated. Exports/shares a CUPS printer to a Samba server using the supplied printer/PPD and Samba credentials, optionally logging to logfile. Returns nonzero on success and 0 on failure (conventional C-style pattern; exact semantics not documented here).
requirements: dest should be a valid destination/printer name.
ppd should reference a valid PPD file path for the printer.
samba_server, samba_user, and samba_password should be valid strings acceptable to the Samba environment.
logfile, if provided, must be a valid FILE* opened for writing/appending; passing NULL may disable logging (behavior not explicitly documented).
Function is deprecated; use modern printing/sharing mechanisms where possible.
Caller must check the return value and handle failures appropriately.

functions.name: cupsAdminGetServerSettings
functions.description: Retrieves current CUPS server settings as an array of name/value options. On success, populates num_settings with the count and settings with a dynamically allocated array of cups_option_t. Returns nonzero on success, 0 on failure. Typical usage: establish an HTTP connection to the server, call this function, then iterate the returned options and free them when done.
requirements: http must be a valid/initialized connection to the target CUPS server.
num_settings must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of options.
settings must be a non-NULL pointer to a cups_option_t*; on success it will point to allocated storage.
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned options array using the matching CUPS free routine (commonly cupsFreeOptions) after use (inferred from CUPS option APIs).
Caller must check the return value; a 0 return indicates failure and output parameters may be unspecified.

functions.name: cupsAdminSetServerSettings
functions.description: Applies the provided list of server settings (name/value options) to the CUPS server. Returns nonzero on success, 0 on failure. Typical usage: build an array of cups_option_t (e.g., with cupsAddOption), then call this with the HTTP connection, the count, and the array.
requirements: http must be a valid/initialized connection to the target CUPS server.
num_settings must be >= 0 and correspond to the number of elements in settings.
settings must point to an array of at least num_settings cups_option_t entries prepared for setting (names/values initialized).
Caller must check the return value to detect and handle failures.
Options should use valid server setting names and values recognized by the CUPS server (implied by purpose).

functions.name: cupsGetDevices
functions.signature: ipp_status_t cupsGetDevices(http_t *http, int timeout, const char *include_schemes, const char *exclude_schemes, cups_device_cb_t callback, void *user_data);
functions.description: Deprecated. Enumerates available print devices from the CUPS server and invokes callback for each discovered device, passing classification, IDs, descriptive fields, URI, and user_data. Returns an IPP status code indicating the result of the request. Typical usage: provide an HTTP connection, a timeout in seconds, optional include/exclude scheme filters, and a non-NULL callback to receive devices.
requirements: http must be a valid/initialized CUPS HTTP connection.
timeout should be >= 0 (commonly seconds to wait for discovery).
include_schemes and exclude_schemes may be NULL or strings specifying URI schemes to include/exclude (format not specified here; commonly comma-separated).
callback must be a valid function pointer matching cups_device_cb_t; it will be called zero or more times during enumeration.
user_data is an opaque pointer passed through to each callback invocation.
Caller must inspect the returned ipp_status_t to detect errors.
Function is deprecated; prefer modern device discovery mechanisms/APIs.

functions.name: cupsBackendDeviceURI
functions.description: Returns the device URI associated with the current CUPS backend invocation, derived from the backend’s command-line context (and possibly environment). Typical usage is inside a CUPS backend’s main(), passing the program’s argv to obtain the target device URI for the job or discovery context. Notes: The exact source of the URI (arguments vs. environment) and lifetime/ownership of the returned pointer are not documented here; treat them as unknown and avoid modifying the returned string.
requirements: argv must be a valid, NULL-terminated array of pointers as provided to main(int argc, char **argv).
Each argv[i] that is accessed by the function must point to a valid, NUL-terminated C string (callers should pass the original argv unmodified).
Call from within a CUPS backend context; behavior and meaning are otherwise unspecified for non-backend programs.
Do not attempt to free or modify the returned const char * (ownership and lifetime are not documented here).
Return value nullability is not documented in this header; callers should defensively check for NULL before use.

functions.name: cupsBackendReport
functions.signature: void cupsBackendReport(const char *device_scheme, const char *device_uri, const char *device_make_and_model, const char *device_info, const char *device_id, const char *device_location);
functions.description: Reports a discovered device from a CUPS backend during device discovery, emitting a standardized record that CUPS will consume. Typical usage is in a backend’s discovery/list mode: call once per device with the device’s URI and metadata (make/model, info, IEEE-1284 device ID, and location). Notes: Output destination and formatting are not documented here; by convention CUPS backends write discovery lines to standard output for cups-deviced to parse.
requirements: All parameters must be valid, non-NULL, NUL-terminated strings.
device_scheme should identify the backend/device scheme (e.g., "usb", "socket", "ipp").
device_uri should be a valid CUPS device URI string (scheme-specific; begins with a scheme followed by ":").

device_make_and_model, device_info, device_id, and device_location should describe the device; empty strings may be used if specific data is unavailable (nullability is not indicated, so prefer non-NULL, possibly empty).
Call from a CUPS backend in device discovery/listing context; calling during normal print-job processing may have no effect or be inappropriate.
The function does not return a status; callers should not assume synchronous validation of parameters beyond best-effort reporting.
